<!-- nota-1: body_md -->
\label{nota:ccH}
We denote by $\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d}\subseteq\mathcal{H}_{g,d}$ the open substack parametrising maps $\theta\colon C\to L$ admitting at least one simple branch value in $L$.

For all $h\ge0$ and all divisors $e\mid d$ with $e<d$, we denote by $\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d}\subseteq\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d}$ the locally closed substack parametrising maps $\theta\colon C\to L$
that satisfy the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\theta$ factors as a composition $C\to C'\xrightarrow{\theta'} L$ with $C'$ of genus $h$ and $\theta'$ of degree $e$;
\item $f$ does not factor through a map to $L$ of degree strictly between $e$ and $d$.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end nota-1 -->
<!-- nota-2: body_md -->
\label{nota:rho}
We abbreviate $\rho(h,e,d)=(h+e-1)(d/e-1)\ge0$.
<!-- end nota-2 -->
<!-- athm-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:A}
Let $d\ge2$. Then there exist constants $I_d,J_d>0$, only depending on $d$, such that for $g\ge1$ there is an isomorphism of rational vector spaces
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:thmA}
H^*(|\mathcal{H}_{g,d}^{\mathrm{top}}|;\mathbb{Q})\cong\bigoplus_{\overset{h\ge0}{1\le e<d,\ e\mid d}} H^{*-4\rho(h,e,d)}(|\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d}^{\mathrm{top}}|;\mathbb{Q})
\end{equation}
in the range of cohomological degrees $*<(2(g+d-1)-J_d)/I_d$.
<!-- end athm-1 -->
<!-- rem-1: body_md -->
For fixed $g\ge1$ only finitely many summands in \eqref{eq:thmA} may contribute non-trivially in the given range of cohomological degrees.
<!-- end rem-1 -->
<!-- rem-2: body_md -->
Our proof of Theorem \ref{thm:A} relies on the validity of homology stability for Hurwitz spaces with monodromies in $\mathfrak{S}_d$. To the best of our knowledge, besides the case $d=2$, the only results in the literature that may be applied in our context are given by the recent work of Landesman--Levy \cite{LL1,LL2}, and in particular \cite[Theorem 1.4.9]{LL2}.
We gather in Notation \ref{nota:goodconstantsIJ} a precise list of properties that the constants $I_d,J_d$ are required to satisfy to guarantee the validity of Theorem \ref{thm:A} and of all other results in the article involving constants ``$I$'' and ``$J$''.
<!-- end rem-2 -->
<!-- rem-3: body_md -->
In their works \cite{CL1,CL2}, Canning--Larson partially shift the focus from $\mathcal{H}_{g,4}$ to the open substack $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{nf}}_{g,4}\subseteq\mathcal{H}_{g,4}$ parametrising those degree 4 maps $\theta\colon C\to L$ that do not factor as a composition of two maps of degree 2: they show that the Chow ring of $\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{nf}}_{g,4}$ is tautological in a stable range, and compute this Chow ring in a stable range. Up to the mild\footnote{This modification consists in removing a high codimension closed substack, so it does not affect Chow or cohomology groups in a stable range. See Example \ref{ex:ccHcH}.} modification imposing the presence of at least one simple branch value, this corresponds to our substack $\mathfrak{F}_{0,1}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,4}$. 
We hope that the splitting in Theorem \ref{thm:A}, though at the level of cohomology and not of Chow rings, may serve as evidence of the inherent obstacles that factoring maps give rise to; in particular, it would be  interesting if there were a splitting as in Theorem \ref{thm:A} for rational Chow rings, or even better, a splitting at the motivic level.
<!-- end rem-3 -->
<!-- nota-3: body_md -->
\label{nota:upsilon}
We abbreviate $\upsilon(g,l,h)=g-1-(h-1)l$.
<!-- end nota-3 -->
<!-- nota-4: body_md -->
\label{nota:universal_curve}
We denote by $\mathfrak{p}_h\colon\mathcal{C}_h\to\mathfrak{M}_h$ the universal genus $h$ curve, and by
$\mathfrak{p}_{h,e}\colon\mathcal{C}_{h,e}\to\mathcal{H}_{h,e}$ its pullback along the forgetful map $\varepsilon_{h,e}\colon\mathcal{H}_{h,e}\to\mathfrak{M}_h$ sending $(\theta\colon C\to L)\mapsto C$.
<!-- end nota-4 -->
<!-- athm-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:B}
Let $d\ge2$ and let $1\le e<d$ be a divisor of $d$. Then there exist constants $I_{d/e},J_{d/e}>0$, only depending on $d/e$, such that for all $g\ge1$ and $h\ge0$ there is a map of rational spectra
\[
|\mathcal{H}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}|_*\left(\int_{|\mathfrak{p}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}|}\mathcal{A}(d/e)\right)_{2\upsilon(g,d/e,h)}\to |\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d}^{\mathrm{top}}|_*\mathbb{Q}
\]
inducing an isomorphism on homotopy groups $\pi_*$ in degrees 
\[
*>-(2\upsilon(g,d/e,h)-J_{d/e})/I_{d/e}.
\]
In particular we have an isomorphism
\[
H^*\left(|\mathcal{H}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}|;\int_{|\mathfrak{p}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}|}\mathcal{A}(d/e)\right)_{2\upsilon(g,d/e,h)}\cong H^*(|\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d}^{\mathrm{top}}|;\mathbb{Q})
\]
in cohomological degrees $*<(2\upsilon(g,d/e,h)-J_{d/e})/I_{d/e}$.
<!-- end athm-2 -->
<!-- acor-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:C}
Combining Theorems \ref{thm:A} and \ref{thm:B} we obtain the following isomorphism of $\mathbb{Q}$-vector spaces, holding in degrees $*<(2(g+d-1)-J_d)/I_d$:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:put_together}
H^*(|\mathcal{H}_{g,d}^{\mathrm{top}}|;\mathbb{Q})\cong\bigoplus_{\overset{h\ge0}{1\le e<d,\ e\mid d}} H^{*-4\rho(h,e,d)}\left(|\mathcal{H}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}|;\int_{|\mathfrak{p}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}|}\mathcal{A}(d/e)\right)_{2\upsilon(g,d/e,h)}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end acor-1 -->
<!-- rem-4: body_md -->
\label{rem:ring_structures?}
The stable cohomology isomorphisms provided in Corollary \ref{cor:C} are isomorphisms of $\mathbb{Q}$-vector spaces, but are not multiplicative. It would be interesting to understand the ring structure on $H^*(|\mathcal{H}_{g,d}^{\mathrm{top}}|;\mathbb{Q})$, and to determine whether also the ring structure stabilises for $g\to\infty$.
<!-- end rem-4 -->
<!-- athm-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:D}
For $h\ge0$, $c\ge2$ and for all $n\ge0$, the map
\[
\xi_{l,h}\cdot-\colon \left(\int_{|\mathfrak{p}_h^{\mathrm{top}}|}\mathcal{A}(l)\right)_n\to  \left(\int_{|\mathfrak{p}_h^{\mathrm{top}}|}\mathcal{A}(l)\right)_{n+1}
\]
of rational parametrised spectra over $|\mathfrak{M}_h^{\mathrm{top}}|$
is a fibrewise equivalence on $\pi_*$ for $*>-n$. Restricting along $|\varepsilon_{e,h}^{\mathrm{top}}|$ and computing cohomology, we obtain an isomorphism
\[ H^*\left(|\mathcal{H}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}|;\int_{|\mathfrak{p}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}|}\mathcal{A}(l)\right)_n\cong
H^*\left(|\mathcal{H}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}|;\int_{|\mathfrak{p}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}|}\mathcal{A}(l)\right)_{n+1}
\]
in cohomological degrees $*<n$, for all $e\ge1$.
<!-- end athm-3 -->
<!-- athm-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:E}
For an oriented closed surface $\Sigma$ of genus $h\ge0$ and for $n\ge0$ there is a $\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma)$-equivariant equivalence of rational spectra
\[
\begin{split}
\left(\int_{|\Sigma|}\mathcal{A}(l)\right)_n&\simeq|\mathrm{Conf}(\Sigma;M_l)_n|_*\mathbb{Q}\quad\text{ for }l=2,3;\\
\left(\int_{|\Sigma|}\mathcal{A}(l)\right)_n&\simeq\bigoplus_{a+2b=n}|\mathrm{Conf}(\Sigma;M_l)_{a,b}|_*\mathbb{Q}\ [-2b]\quad\text{ for }l=4,5.
\end{split}
\]
<!-- end athm-4 -->
<!-- acor-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:F}
Let $g\ge0$; for $d=2,3,5$ we have stable isomorphisms of graded $\mathbb{Q}$-vector spaces as follows:
\[
\begin{split}
H^*(|\mathcal{H}_{g,2}^{\mathrm{top}}|;\mathbb{Q})&\cong H^*(|\mathrm{Conf}(\mathfrak{p}_0^{\mathrm{top}},M_2)_{2g+2}|;\mathbb{Q});\\
H^*(|\mathcal{H}_{g,3}^{\mathrm{top}}|;\mathbb{Q})&\cong H^*(|\mathrm{Conf}(\mathfrak{p}_0^{\mathrm{top}},M_3)_{2g+4}|;\mathbb{Q});\\
H^*(|\mathcal{H}_{g,5}^{\mathrm{top}}|;\mathbb{Q})&\cong \bigoplus_{a+2b=2g+8}H^{*-2b}(|\mathrm{Conf}(\mathfrak{p}_0^{\mathrm{top}},M_5)_{a,b}|;\mathbb{Q}),
\end{split}
\]
whereas for $d=4$ we have that $H^*(|\mathcal{H}_{g,4}^{\mathrm{top}}|;\mathbb{Q})$ is stably isomorphic to
\[
\begin{split}
&\bigoplus_{h\ge0} H^{*-4(h+1)}(|\mathrm{Conf}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,2}^{\mathrm{top}},M_2)_{2g+2-4h}|;\mathbb{Q})\\
\oplus& \bigoplus_{a+2b=2g+6}H^{*-2b}(|\mathrm{Conf}(\mathfrak{p}_0^{\mathrm{top}},M_4)_{a,b}|;\mathbb{Q}).
\end{split}
\]
Precisely, the stable isomorphism associated with $d=2,3,4,5$ holds in the range of cohomological degrees $*<(2(g+d-1)-J_d)/I_d$, .
<!-- end acor-2 -->
<!-- rem-5: body_md -->
\label{rem:hyperelliptic}
For $h\ge2$ we remark that the stack $\mathcal{H}_{h,2}$ can be identified with the hyperelliptic locus inside $\mathfrak{M}_h$ along the map $\varepsilon_{h,2}\colon\mathcal{H}_{h,2}\to\mathfrak{M}_h$; in particular this is an equivalence for $h=2$. For $h\le1$ the map $\varepsilon_{h,2}$ has positive-dimensional fibres.

For arbitrary $l$ we also remark that $|\mathrm{Conf}(\mathfrak{p}_0^{\mathrm{top}},M_l)|$ is equivalent to the homotopy quotient $|\mathrm{Conf}(S^2,M_l)|\sslash\mathrm{Homeo}^+(S^2)\simeq|\mathrm{Conf}(S^2,M_l)|\sslash\mathrm{SO}(3)$.
<!-- end rem-5 -->
<!-- rem-6: body_md -->
\label{rem:Zheng}
For $d=2$ it is a classical result that $H^*(|\mathcal{H}_{g,2}^{\mathrm{top}}|)\cong \mathbb{Q}$ for any $g\ge1$, in particular we know the entire cohomology ring. For $d=3$, Zheng \cite{Zheng} proved that $H^*(|\mathcal{H}_{g,3}^{\mathrm{top}}|)$ agrees with $\mathbb{Q}[\kappa_1]/\kappa_1^3$ in degrees $*\le \lfloor g/4\rfloor$; here we denote by $\kappa_1$ the pullback of the first Mumford--Morita--Miller class along $|\varepsilon_{g,3}^{\mathrm{top}}|\colon|\mathcal{H}_{g,3}^{\mathrm{top}}|\to|\mathfrak{M}_g^{\mathrm{top}}|$. Corollary \ref{cor:F} partially recovers these results (see Subsection \ref{subsec:oddexamples}), but only in the stable ranges provided by the constants $I_d,J_d$, and only at the level of vector spaces: the multiplicative structure, as well as the the identification of the generators as powers of $\kappa_1$, can probably be recovered too with some additional effort. In particular, for $d=3$, Zheng's range $*<\lfloor g/4\rfloor$ is better than the current best available range relying on the work of Landesman--Levy.
<!-- end rem-6 -->
<!-- rem-7: body_md -->
For $l\le5$ the algebra $\mathcal{A}(l)$ can be generated with at most two elements and it admits a monomial presentation; this allows us to make a fairly simple analysis of its factorisation homology over a surface $\Sigma$ and obtain Theorem \ref{thm:D}. A complete presentation of $\mathcal{A}(l)$ is known for $l\le10$ \cite{BCP:Hilb}; for $6\le l\le10$ we have that $\mathcal{A}(l)$ is minimally generated by at least three elements and admits no monomial presentation, making the analysis of its factorisation homology harder.
<!-- end rem-7 -->
<!-- rem-8: body_md -->
The presence of odd-dimensional classes implies that for $d=4,5$, the stable rational cohomology of $|\mathcal{H}_{g,d}^{\mathrm{top}}|$ is not fully algebraic, i.e., not in the image of the cycle class map from the Chow ring. This is in stark contrast with the cases $d=2,3$, as seen in Remark \ref{rem:Zheng}, as well as with the situation for $\mathfrak{M}_g$, in which the stable rational cohomology is fully tautological \cite{MadsenWeiss}.
<!-- end rem-8 -->
<!-- defn-1: body_md -->
\label{defn:algHurstack}
Recall Notation \ref{nota:universal_curve}.
For $g,h\ge0$ and $l\ge1$ we denote by
$\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_h)$
the moduli stack of degree $l$ maps $\theta\colon C\to D$ between smooth connected complex projective curves, with $C$ of genus $g$ and $D$ of genus $h$. When $h=0$ we abbreviate $\mathcal{H}_{g,l}:=\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_0)$, as in the introduction.

We denote by $q_{g,l,h}\colon \mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_h)\to\mathfrak{M}_h$ the forgetful map sending $(\theta\colon C\to D)\mapsto D$.
It is smooth, and its fibre over a curve $D$ of genus $h$ is the moduli stack $\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(D)$ of genus $g$ degree $l$ covers of $D$.

For a family $\mathfrak{p}\colon \mathcal{E}\to\mathcal{B}$ of curves of genus $h$ over a stack $\mathcal{B}$, classified by a map $\varepsilon\colon \mathcal{B}\to \mathfrak{M}_h$, we denote by $\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p})$ the fibre product
\[
\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p})=\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_h)\times_{\mathfrak{M}_h} \mathcal{B},
\]
computed along the maps $\varepsilon$ and $q_{g,l,h}$.
<!-- end defn-1 -->
<!-- ex-1: body_md -->
\label{ex:cHglhe}
For $e\ge1$ and $h\ge0$ we may consider, as in Notation \ref{nota:universal_curve}, the map $\mathfrak{p}_{h,e}\colon\mathcal{C}_{h,e}\to\mathcal{H}_{h,e}$ classified by the map $\varepsilon_{h,e}\colon\mathcal{H}_{h,e}\to\mathfrak{M}_h$. For $g\ge0$ and $l\ge1$ we then have that $\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})$ is the moduli stack of sequences of maps $C\to D\to L$ of curves of genera $g,h,0$ respectively, with $C\to D$ and $D\to L$ of degrees $l$ and $e$ respectively.
<!-- end ex-1 -->
<!-- nota-5: body_md -->
\label{nota:qglhe}
In the setting of Example \ref{ex:cHglhe} we denote by $q_{g,l,h,e}\colon\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})\to\mathcal{H}_{h,e}$ the map sending $(C\to D\to L)\mapsto (D\to L)$.
<!-- end nota-5 -->
<!-- rem-9: body_md -->
\label{rem:cHgdDMstack}
The case $l=1$ is degenerate and only included in Definition \ref{defn:algHurstack} for uniform notation: the stack $\mathcal{H}_{g,1}(\mathfrak{p}_h)$ is non-empty if and only if $g=h$, in which case it is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{M}_h$ along $q_{g,1,h}$.

For $l\ge2$, the stack $\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_h)$ is non-empty if and only if the number $\upsilon(g,l,h)$ from Notation \ref{nota:upsilon} is $\ge0$. In this case $2\upsilon(g,l,h)$ counts, with multiplicity, the number of branch values of a degree $l$ map $\theta\colon C\to D$ from a genus $g$ curve to a genus $h$ curve.

We also observe that a degree $l$ map $\theta\colon C\to D$ between curves of genera $g$ and $h$ admits finitely many automorphisms unless either $g=h\le1$. Consequently, $\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_h)$ is a Deligne--Mumford stack whenever $g\ge2$, or $g=1$ and $h=0$.

For a curve $D$ of genus $h$, the stack $\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(D)$ is a (possibly empty) Deligne--Mumford stack for all $g\ge0$ and $l\ge1$.
<!-- end rem-9 -->
<!-- rem-10: body_md -->
This remark is the fruit of a conversation with Aaron Landesman.
If $d$ is a prime number and $g>(d-1)^2$, then the map $\varepsilon_{g,d}\colon\mathcal{H}_{g,d}\to\mathfrak{M}_g$ is an inclusion, with image the locus of $d$-gonal curves, i.e. those curves of genus $g$ admitting some degree $d$ map to a genus 0 curve, without a specific choice of this datum. In other words, a degree $d$ map $\theta\colon C\to \mathbb{P}^1$, if it exists, is unique up to automorphism of $\mathbb{P}^1$.

To see this, we observe that if $\theta_1,\theta_2\colon C\to \mathbb{P}^1$ are two maps of degree $d$, they combine into a map $\theta_1\times\theta_2\colon C\to \mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$. The image of this map is an irreducible, but possibly singular curve $C'\subseteq\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$ of bidegree $(e,e)$ for some divisor $e\mid d$, and the map $\theta_1\times\theta_2\colon C\to C'$ has degree $d/e$. If $e=1$ then $C'$ is the graph of an automorphism of $\mathbb{P}^1$, which means that $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ differ by an automorphism of $\mathbb{P}^1$. If $e=d$ then $C$ is the normalisation of $C'$, and $C'$, being a (possibly singular) curve of bidegree $(d,d)$ in $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$, has genus $\le(d-1)^2$.
<!-- end rem-10 -->
<!-- nota-6: body_md -->
For an oriented closed topological surface $\Sigma$, i.e. a compact 2-dimensional topological manifold without boundary, we denote by $\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma)$ the topological group of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of $\Sigma$, endowed with the compact-open topology.
<!-- end nota-6 -->
<!-- ex-2: body_md -->
To see how this double step sheds topological light into our problem, let us first remind what happens for the algebraic stack $\mathfrak{M}_g$ for $g\ge0$. The topological stack $\mathfrak{M}_g^{\mathrm{top}}$ associates with a topological space the groupoid $\mathfrak{M}_g^{\mathrm{top}}(X)$ of smooth oriented fibre bundles $p\colon C\to X$ with fibre a (real) surface of genus $g$, together with a continuous choice of Riemann structures on fibres; morphisms are given by bundle isomorphisms that are fibrewise holomorphic. If we further pass to the underlying homotopy type $|\mathfrak{M}_g^{\mathrm{top}}|$, we obtain the homotopy type $\mathbf{B}\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma)$ of the classifying space of $\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma)$, where $\Sigma$ is a closed oriented topological surface of genus $g$; this is also a classifying space for fibre bundles with genus $g$ oriented surfaces as fibres.
<!-- end ex-2 -->
<!-- defn-2: body_md -->
\label{defn:Bra}
Let $\Sigma$ be a closed connected oriented topological surface and let 
$A\subseteq B\subseteq \Sigma$ be finite subsets, with $\#A\le1$.
Let $l\ge2$. The topological stack 
$\mathrm{Bra}^l_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} A{\,\text{\'et}\,} B}$ 
associates with a space $X$ the groupoid whose objects are sequences $(Y,p,\theta,\mathbf{t})$ where $Y$ is a space, $p\colon Y\to X$ and $\theta\colon Y\to\Sigma$ are maps, and $\mathbf{t}\colon X\times A\times\underline{l}\cong \theta^{-1}(A)$ is a homeomorphism, satisfying the following properties:
\begin{itemize}
\item $p$ is a fibre bundle whose fibres are possibly disconnected closed surfaces;
\item for each $x\in X$ the restricted map $\theta\colon p^{-1}(x)\to \Sigma$ is a topological $l$-fold branched cover; that is, it is proper \'etale of degree $l$ away from a finite subset of $p^{-1}(x)$ of \emph{branch points}, and it can be modeled up to local homeomorphism by the map $\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$, $z\mapsto z^r$ near the branch points for some $2\le r\le l$; we require moreover that $p^{-1}(x)\to\Sigma$ is \'etale over $B$;
\item the composition $p\circ\mathbf{t}\colon X\times A\times\underline{l}\to X$
agrees with the product projection.
\end{itemize}
Morphisms in $\mathrm{Bra}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} A{\,\text{\'et}\,} B}^l(X)$ are homeomorphisms $Y\cong Y'$ over $X\times \Sigma$ and under $X\times A\times\underline{l}$.
When $A=\emptyset$ we remove $A$ and $\mathbf{t}$ from the notation, whereas when $A=\left\{a\right\}$ we write ${\,\text{rel}\,} a$. Similarly, when $A=B$ we remove $B$ from the notation.

We denote by $\mathrm{CBra}^l_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} A{\,\text{\'et}\,} B}\subseteq\mathrm{Bra}^l_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} A{\,\text{\'et}\,} B}$ the topological substack spanned at $X$ by those sequences $(Y,p,\theta,\mathbf{t})$ such that $p$ has connected fibres.
For $g\ge0$ we denote by $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} A{\,\text{\'et}\,} B}\subseteq\mathrm{CBra}^l_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} A{\,\text{\'et}\,} B}$ the topological substack spanned at $X$ by those sequences $(Y,p,\theta,\mathbf{t})$ such that fibres of $p$ are connected genus $g$ surfaces.
<!-- end defn-2 -->
<!-- defn-3: body_md -->
\label{defn:smallloop}
Given a finite subset $P\subseteq \Sigma\setminus\left\{a\right\}$, a \emph{small loop} is an element in $\pi_1(\Sigma\setminus P;a)$ whose conjugacy class is represented by an unbased (or free) simple loop $\gamma$ in $\Sigma\setminus P$ that spins once, clockwise\footnote{With respect to the orientation of $\Sigma$.}, around a single point of $P$.
<!-- end defn-3 -->
<!-- defn-4: body_md -->
\label{defn:norm}
The \emph{norm} of a permutation $\sigma\in\mathfrak{S}_l$, also known as its \emph{absolute length}, is the minimum $r\ge0$ such that $\sigma$ may be written as a product of $r$ transpositions.
Equivalently, if $\sigma$ consists of $m$ cycles, then $N(\sigma)=l-m$.
<!-- end defn-4 -->
<!-- nota-7: body_md -->
\label{nota:fP}
We denote by $\mathfrak{P}(l)$ the set of all partitions $\lambda\vdash l$, i.e. the set of conjugacy classes in $\mathfrak{S}_l$.
For $\lambda\in\mathfrak{P}(l)$ we denote by $N(\lambda)=N(\sigma)$ for any $\sigma\in\lambda$. We let $\mathfrak{P}(l)_+\subseteq\mathfrak{P}(l)$ denote the subset of non-discrete partitions, or equivalently, the set of conjugacy class of non-identity elements in $\mathfrak{S}_l$.
<!-- end nota-7 -->
<!-- nota-8: body_md -->
\label{nota:Nzphi}
Let $P\subseteq\Sigma\setminus\left\{a\right\}$ be a finite subset, let $\varphi\colon\pi_1(\Sigma\setminus P;a)\to\mathfrak{S}_l$ be a group homomorphism, and let $z\in P$. We write $N(z,\varphi):=N(\varphi(\gamma))\ge0$ for any small loop $\gamma$ spinning around $z$. We observe that up to conjugation $\varphi(\gamma)$ only depends on $z$, hence also $N(z,\varphi)$ only depends on $z$.
<!-- end nota-8 -->
<!-- defn-5: body_md -->
\label{defn:fUsubset}
Let $(P,\varphi)\in\mathrm{Bra}^l_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} a}$, expand $P=\left\{z_1,\dots,z_k\right\}$, and let $\underline{U}=(U_1,\dots,U_k)$ be open discs in $\Sigma\setminus\left\{a\right\}$ with disjoint closures, with $U_i$ intersecting $P$ only in $z_i$. We associate with the data $P,\varphi,\underline{U}$ the subset
\[
\mathfrak{U}(P,\varphi,\underline{U})\subseteq\mathrm{Bra}^l_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} a}
\]
consisting of all pairs $(P',\varphi')$ satisfying the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $P'\subseteq U_1\cup\dots\cup U_k$ and $P'$ interesects each $U_i$ in at least one point;
\item the following composite group homomorphism
agrees with $\varphi$:
\[
\pi_1(\Sigma\setminus P;a)\overset{\cong}{\leftarrow}\pi_1(\Sigma\setminus\underline{U};a)\to\pi_1(\Sigma\setminus P';a)\xrightarrow{\varphi'}\mathfrak{S}_l;
\]
\item for all $1\le i\le k$ the following equality holds:
\[
N(z_i,\varphi)=\sum_{z'\in P'\cap U_i}N(z',\varphi').
\]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-5 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:orbifold}
Let $\Sigma$ be a connected oriented closed surface of genus $h\ge0$, let $l\ge2$ and $g\ge0$, and let $A\subseteq B\subseteq\Sigma$ be finite subsets as in Definition \ref{defn:Bra}. Recall Notation \ref{nota:upsilon}.
Then the topological stack $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} A{\,\text{\'et}\,} B}$ 
is
\begin{enumerate}
\item empty, if $\upsilon(g,l,h)<0$;
\item an oriented orbifold of real dimension $4\upsilon(g,l,h)$, if $\upsilon(g,l,h)\ge0$; 
\item a manifold, if moreover $A\neq\emptyset$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Since $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} A{\,\text{\'et}\,} B}$ is an open topological substack of $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} A}$, it suffices to consider the case $A=B$.

We first address point (1): if $\upsilon(g,l,h)=g-1-(h-1)l<0$, then the Riemann--Hurwitz formula prevents the existence of a degree $l$ branched cover map between oriented topological closed surfaces of genera $g$ and $h$. From now on we assume $\upsilon(g,l,h)\ge0$, and abbreviate $\upsilon=\upsilon(g,l,h)$.

We next address point (3): let $A=\left\{a\right\}$, let $(P,\varphi)\in\mathrm{Bra}^l_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} a}$, expand $P=\left\{z_1,\dots,z_k\right\}$ and let $\underline{U}=(U_1,\dots,U_k)$ as in Definition \ref{defn:fUsubset}. Fix $k$ small loops $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_k\subseteq\Sigma\setminus\underline{U}$ based at $a$, with $\gamma_i$ spinning clockwise around $U_i$. Let $\sigma_i=\varphi(\gamma_i)\in\mathfrak{S}_l$, and consider $\sigma_i$ as an element of the partially multiplicative quandle $\mathfrak{S}_l^{\mathrm{geo}}$ from \cite[Definition 7.1]{Bianchi:Hur1}, as well as an element of the multiplicative completion $\widehat{\mathfrak{S}_l^{\mathrm{geo}}}$ of the latter. Then a straightforward generalisation of \cite[Proposition 5.1]{Bianchi:Hur2} identifies $\mathfrak{U}(P,\varphi,\underline{U})$ up to homeomorphism with an open subset of the product $\prod_{i=1}^k\mathrm{Hur}^\Delta(\mathfrak{S}_l^{\mathrm{geo}})_{\sigma_i}$; here $\mathrm{Hur}^\Delta(\mathfrak{S}_l^{\mathrm{geo}})$ is the Hurwitz space with collisions from \cite[Definition 6.13]{Bianchi:Hur1}, and 
$\mathrm{Hur}^\Delta(\mathfrak{S}_l^{\mathrm{geo}})_{\sigma_i}$ is the connected component corresponding to $\sigma_i\in\widehat{\mathfrak{S}_l^{\mathrm{geo}}}$. 
By \cite[Theorem B]{Bianchi:Hur4} we then have that $\mathrm{Hur}^\Delta(\mathfrak{S}_l^{\mathrm{geo}})_{\sigma_i}$ is naturally an open complex manifold of complex dimension $N(\sigma_i)=N(z_i,\varphi)$, in particular it carries a canonical orientation. It follows that $\mathfrak{U}(P,\varphi,\underline{U})$, and hence the entire $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} a}$, is naturally a
topological oriented manifold of real dimension $4\upsilon=2\sum_{i=1}^kN(z_i,\varphi)$.

We finally address point (2) following \cite[§4.4]{DasPetersen}; it suffices to consider the case $A=\emptyset$.
For varying $a\in\Sigma$, the substacks $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{\'et}\,} a}$ give an open cover of $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_\Sigma$. We may now consider the action of $\mathfrak{S}_l$ on the manifold $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} a}$ given as follows: a permutation $\sigma\in \mathfrak{S}_l$ sends a point $(Y,\theta,\mathbf{t})\in\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} a}$ to $(Y,p,\theta,\sigma\circ\mathbf{t})$. The action is orientation preserving, and the quotient orbifold may be identified with $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{\'et}\,} a}$, which is in particular indeed an oriented orbifold.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:Braorbifold}
Let $\Sigma$ be a closed connected oriented surface of genus $h\ge0$, and let $g\ge0$ and $l\ge2$ be such that $\upsilon(g,l,h)\ge0$. Then the coarse space $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$ associated with the Deligne--Mumford topological stack $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_\Sigma$ is an oriented rational homology manifold of dimension $4\upsilon(g,l,h)$.

In particular, by Poincar\'e--Lefschetz duality, we have a $\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma)$-equivariant equivalence of rational spectra
\[
|\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}|_*\mathbb{Q}\simeq(|\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}|,\infty)_!\mathbb{Q}\ [-4\upsilon(g,l,h)].
\]
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
This follows directly from the fact that $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma}$ is an oriented orbifold of said real dimension.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- rem-11: body_md -->
We expect $|\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top}}_\mathrm{vcrs}|$ to agree with the underlying homotopy type an algebraic stack ``$\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})_\mathrm{vcrs}$'' of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$, parametrising degree $e$ maps $\theta\colon D\to L$ from a curve of genus $h$ to a curve of genus $0$, together with an isomorphism class of genus $g$, degree $l$ covers of $D$. We will not need this algebraic perspective in the following.
<!-- end rem-11 -->
<!-- prop-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:defnTheta}
Let $\Sigma$ be a closed connected oriented topological surface of genus $h\ge0$, let $l\ge2$, and let $g\ge0$. Assume $\upsilon(g,l,h)\ge1$. Then there is a well-defined and $\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma)$-equivariant map of rational spectra
\[
\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma\colon\left(\int_{\Sigma}\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)\right)_{2\upsilon(g,l,h)}\to(|\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}|,\infty)_!\mathbb{Q}.
\]
<!-- end prop-2 -->
<!-- rem-12: body_md -->
\label{rem:upsilonzero}
If $\upsilon(g,l,h)=0$, then the source and target of the map $\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma$ are canonically equivalent to $\mathbb{Q}$: we then just let $\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma$ be the identity of $\mathbb{Q}$. If $\upsilon(g,l,h)<0$ then both source and target of $\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma$ are zero: we then let $\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma$ be the zero map.
<!-- end rem-12 -->
<!-- defn-6: body_md -->
We denote by $\mathrm{Fin}$ the category of finite sets, endowed with the coproduct (disjoint union) symmetric monoidal structure; we let $\mathrm{FS}$ denote the subcategory of finite non-empty sets and surjective maps; $\mathrm{FS}$ lacks a monoidal unit, but we may still consider it as a non-unital symmetric monoidal subcategory of $\mathrm{Fin}$. For a homotopy type $Y$ we denote by $\mathrm{Fin}_{/Y}$ the $\infty$-category of finite sets with a map to $Y$, and by $\mathrm{FS}_{/Y}$ the fibre product of $\infty$-categories $\mathrm{FS}\times_{\mathrm{Fin}}\mathrm{Fin}_{/Y}$.
<!-- end defn-6 -->
<!-- ex-3: body_md -->
Our motivating examples for $\mathcal{C}$ are $\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}$, the $\infty$-category of rational spectra, and $\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}^\mathbb{N}\coloneqq\mathrm{Fun}(\mathbb{N},\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q})$, the $\infty$-category of functors from $\mathbb{N}$ to $\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}$, which we refer to as \emph{graded spectra}. Here $\mathbb{N}$ denotes the symmetric monoidal groupoid whose objects are natural numbers, and whose only morphisms are identities; $\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}$ is endowed with the symmetric monoidal structure given by tensor product of spectra, and $\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}^\mathbb{N}$ with the symmetric monoidal structure given by Day convolution. There is a symmetric monoidal functor $\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}^\mathbb{N}\to\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}$ sending a graded spectrum $(\omega_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\in\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}^\mathbb{N}$ to the direct sum $\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\omega_n\in\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}$; we refer to it as the functor forgetting grading.
Our motivating examples for $R$ are the algebras $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l),\mathcal{A}(l)\in\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}^\mathbb{N})$, that we shall introduce in Definitions \ref{defn:cAheart} and \ref{defn:cA}, as well as their images in $\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q})$ along the grading forgetful functor.
<!-- end ex-3 -->
<!-- rem-13: body_md -->
\label{rem:FSreduction}
Since we assume that $Y$ is connected, the following hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item the canonical functor $\mathrm{FS}_{/Y}\to\mathrm{Fin}_{/Y}$ is final, and in particular $\int_YR$ agrees with the colimit over $\mathrm{FS}_{/Y}$ of the composite functor $\mathrm{FS}_{/Y}\to\mathrm{Fin}\xrightarrow{R}\mathcal{C}$;
\item if $\mathcal{C}$ is stable and $R\to\mathbbl{1}_\mathcal{C}$ is an augmentation, then we may split $R=\mathbbl{1}_\mathcal{C}\oplus R_+$, where $R_+$ is the augmentation ideal. We may consider $R_+\colon\mathrm{FS}\to\mathcal{C}$ as a non-unital symmetric monoidal functor. Then the colimit over $\mathrm{FS}_{/Y}$ of the composite $\mathrm{FS}_{/Y}\to\mathrm{FS}\xrightarrow{R_+}\mathcal{C}$ computes the fibre of the augmentation $\int_YR\to\int_Y\mathbbl{1}_\mathcal{C}\simeq \mathbbl{1}_\mathcal{C}$.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end rem-13 -->
<!-- defn-7: body_md -->
\label{defn:int}
Let $Y$ be a connected homotopy type and let $I\colon\mathrm{FS}\to\mathcal{C}$ be a non-unital, symmetric monoidal functor with target a presentably symmetric monoidal stable $\infty$-category $\mathcal{C}$. We define
\[
\int_YI\coloneqq \operatorname{colim}(\mathrm{FS}_{/Y}\to\mathrm{Fin}\xrightarrow{I}\mathcal{C})\in\mathcal{C}.
\]
<!-- end defn-7 -->
<!-- nota-9: body_md -->
\label{nota:skeletalFS}
To avoid set theoretic issues, as well as some non-canonical choices in the following, we model the category $\mathrm{FS}$ by its skeletal full subcategory whose objects are finite nonempty subsets of $X$.
<!-- end nota-9 -->
<!-- nota-10: body_md -->
We denote by $\Delta^p=\left\{(t_1,\dots,t_p)\in\mathbb{R}^{p+1}\,|\,t_i\ge0,\ \sum_it_i=1\right\}$ the standard geometric $p$-simplex. For $0\le i\le p$ we denote by $\delta_i\colon\Delta^{p-1}\to\Delta^p$ the $i$\textsuperscript{th} face inclusion. In particular $\delta_0\colon(t_0,\dots,t_{p-1})\mapsto(0,t_0,\dots,t_{p-1})$.

For $p\ge0$ and a singular simplex $s\colon \Delta^p\to X$ we denote by $\alpha(s)=s(1,0,\dots,0)\in X$ the initial vertex.
<!-- end nota-10 -->
<!-- defn-8: body_md -->
\label{defn:SingFS}
We model the $\infty$-category $\mathrm{FS}_{/|X|}$ as the simplicial set $\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X)$ described as follows: for $p\ge0$, a $p$-simplex in $\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_p(X)$ is a choice of:
\begin{itemize}
\item a sequence $\underline{S}=(S_0\twoheadrightarrow \dots\twoheadrightarrow S_p)$ of nonempty finite sets as in Notation \ref{nota:skeletalFS} and surjective maps, i.e. a $p$-simplex in the nerve of $\mathrm{FS}$;
\item a continuous map $s\colon\Delta^p\to X^{S_0}$ such that, for all $1\le i\le p$, there exists a (necessarily unique) dashed map making the following diagram of spaces commute:
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=10]
\Delta^{p-i}\ar[d,"\delta_0^i"]\ar[r,dashed]&X^{S_i}\ar[d,hook,"X^{S_0\twoheadrightarrow S_i}"]\\
\Delta^p\ar[r,"s"]&X^{S_0}.
\end{tikzcd}
\]
\end{itemize}
Face and degeneracy maps in $\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X)$ are given by omitting or repeating the finite subsets $S_i$, and by suitably restricting $s$.
<!-- end defn-8 -->
<!-- defn-9: body_md -->
The simplicial $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space $\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X,I)$ is given in degree $p\ge0$ by
\[
\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_p(X,I)=\bigoplus_{(\underline{S},s)\in\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_p(X)}I^{\otimes S_0}.
\]
For $1\le i\le p$, respectively $0\le j\le p$, the face map $d_i$, respectively the degeneracy map $s_j$, restricts to the identity of $I^{\otimes S_0}$ from the $(\underline{S},s)$-summand to the $d_i(\underline{S},s)$-summand, respectively to the $s_j(\underline{S},s)$-summand.
For $i=0$, instead, it sends the $(\underline{S},s)$-summand $I^{\otimes S_0}$ to the $d_0(\underline{S},s)$-summand $I^{\otimes S_1}$ along the multiplication map $I^{\otimes S_0}\to I^{\otimes S_1}$ induced by the surjection $S_0\twoheadrightarrow S_1$.
<!-- end defn-9 -->
<!-- rem-14: body_md -->
\label{rem:catofsimplices}
The simplicial $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space $\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_p(X,I)$ arises concretely by considering the category of simplices of $\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_p(X,I)$, which we temporarily denote by $W$. There is a functor $W\to\mathrm{Vec}_\mathbb{Q}$ sending $(\underline{S},s)\mapsto I^{\otimes S_0}$, and $\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X,I)$ is the left Kan extension of this functor along the projection $W\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$.
<!-- end rem-14 -->
<!-- defn-10: body_md -->
\label{defn:Ran}
We let $\mathrm{Ran}(X)$ denote the set of all finite nonempty subsets of $X$. For $n\ge1$ we denote by $\mathrm{Ran}_{\le n}(X)\subseteq\mathrm{Ran}(X)$ the subset of those subsets of $X$ having cardinality at most $n$. We topologise $\mathrm{Ran}_{\le n}(X)$ as a quotient of $X^n$, and $\mathrm{Ran}(X)$ as the union $\bigcup_{n\ge1}\mathrm{Ran}_{\le n}(X)$. We denote by $\#\colon\mathrm{Ran}(X)\to\mathbb{N}_{\ge1}$ the lower semicontinuous function assigning to a finite nonempty subset of $X$ its cardinality.

For $k\ge1$ we denote by $\mathrm{Conf}_k(X)\coloneqq\#^{-1}(k)\subseteq\mathrm{Ran}(X)$ the $k$\textsuperscript{th} unordered configuration space of $X$.
<!-- end defn-10 -->
<!-- defn-11: body_md -->
\label{defn:ER}
We let $\mathrm{ERan}_\bullet(X)\subseteq\mathrm{Sing}_\bullet(\mathrm{Ran}(X))$ denote the subsimplicial set spanned at level $p$ by those singular simplices $s\colon\Delta^p\to\mathrm{Ran}(X)$ for which the following property holds: there exist $n_0\ge \dots\ge n_p\in\mathbb{N}_{\ge1}$ such that for all $0\le i\le p$ and all $(0,\dots,0,t_i,\dots,t_p)\in\Delta^p$ with $t_i\neq0$ we have $\#(s(0,\dots,0,t_i,\dots,t_p))=n_i$.
<!-- end defn-11 -->
<!-- rem-15: body_md -->
By \cite[Theorem A.6.4]{HA} we have that $\mathrm{ERan}_\bullet(X)$ is in fact a quasi-category. We believe that the functor of quasi-categories $\kappa$ is in fact final, but refrain from proving this more general statement and focus on proving that it preserves the colimit corresponding to factorisation homology.
<!-- end rem-15 -->
<!-- defn-12: body_md -->
Recall Definition \ref{defn:SingFSR} and Remark \ref{rem:catofsimplices}.
We let $\mathrm{ERan}_\bullet(X,I)$ be the simplicial $\mathbb{Q}$-subvector space of $\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X,I)$ given in degree $p\ge0$ by
\[
\mathrm{ERan}_p(X,I)=\bigoplus_{s\in\mathrm{ERan}_p(X)}I^{\alpha(s)}\subset\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_p(X,I).
\]
We denote by $\kappa^I\colon\mathrm{ERan}_\bullet(X,I)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X,I)$ the canonical inclusion.
<!-- end defn-12 -->
<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:kappaiso}
The map $\kappa^I$ induces a quasi-isomorphism on chain complexes.
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- defn-13: body_md -->
\label{defn:starfiltation}
For $k\ge1$ we let $F_k\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X)$ denote the subsimplicial set spanned by those simplices $(\underline{S},s)$ with $\#S_0\le k$. We obtain a filtration of simplicial sets $F_\star\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X)$ with $F_k\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X)\subseteq F_{k+1}\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X)$. We restrict this filtration along $\kappa$ and obtain a filtration $F_\star\mathrm{ERan}_\bullet(X)$.

Passing to simplicial $\mathbb{Q}$-vector spaces, we also let $F_k\mathrm{Sing}_\bullet^\mathrm{FS}(X,I)$ denote the simplicial $\mathbb{Q}$-subvector space of $\mathrm{Sing}_\bullet^\mathrm{FS}(X,I)$ spanned by those summands corresponding to simplices in $F_k\mathrm{Sing}_\bullet^\mathrm{FS}(X)$. We also restrict this filtration along $\kappa^I$.
<!-- end defn-13 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Since $\kappa^I$ is a filtered map, it suffices to prove it induces a quasi-isomorphism $(F_k/F_{k-1})\kappa^I$ between filtration quotients for all $k\ge1$. Fix $k$ in the following and let $T\subseteq X$ be a fixed set of $k$ elements. 
Using the nerves of the categories $\mathrm{FS}$ and $\mathrm{FS}_{T/}$,
define the auxiliary simplicial set 
\[
\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X)_{T/}\coloneqq\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X)\times_{N_\bullet(\mathrm{FS})}N_\bullet(\mathrm{FS}_{T/}),
\]
and following Remark \ref{rem:catofsimplices} define the auxiliary simplicial $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space $\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X,I)_{T/}$, given as the left Kan extension to $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ of the functor from the category of simplices of $\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X,I)_{T/}$ to $\mathrm{Vec}_\mathbb{Q}$ sending $(\underline{S},s,T\twoheadrightarrow S_0)\mapsto I^{\otimes S_0}$.
Explicitly, we have
\[
\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_p(X,I)_{T/}=\bigoplus_{(\underline{S},s,T\twoheadrightarrow S_0)\in\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_p(X)_{T/}}I^{\otimes S_0}
\]

Define similarly the pullback simplicial set
\[
\mathrm{ERan}_\bullet(X)_{T/}\coloneqq \mathrm{ERan}_\bullet(X)\times_{\mathrm{Sing}_\bullet^\mathrm{FS}(X)}\mathrm{Sing}_\bullet^\mathrm{FS}(X)_{T/}\subseteq\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X)_{T/}
\]
and the auxiliary simplicial $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space $\mathrm{ERan}_\bullet(X,I)_{T/}$, with
\[
\mathrm{ERan}_p(X,I)_{T/}=\bigoplus_{(s,T\twoheadrightarrow \alpha(s))\in\mathrm{ERan}_p(X)_{T/}}R^{\alpha(s)}\subseteq\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X,I)_{T/}.
\]
Then $\kappa^I$ canonically lifts to an injective map of simplicial $\mathbb{Q}$-vector spaces
\[
\kappa^I_{T/}\colon \mathrm{ERan}_\bullet(X,I)_{T/}\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X,I)_{T/},
\]
which we treat as an inclusion. The group $\mathfrak{S}_T$ of automorphisms of $T$ naturally acts on both auxiliary simplicial $\mathbb{Q}$-vector spaces, and $\kappa^I_{T/}$ is $\mathfrak{S}_T$-equivariant.

For $n=k-1,k$ denote by $F_n\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X,I)_{T/}$ the preimage of $F_n\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X,I)$ along the forgetful map $\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X,I)_{T/}\to \mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X,I)$, and define  in a similar way $F_n\mathrm{ERan}_\bullet(X,I)_{T/}$. Then $\kappa^I_{T/}$ is a filtered simplicial $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space map, and upon quotienting the $\mathfrak{S}_T$-action, the simplicial map $(F_k/F_{k-1})\kappa^I_{T/}$ becomes the simplicial map $(F_k/F_{k-1})\kappa^I$. Using that the source and target of $(F_k/F_{k-1})\kappa^I_{T/}$ are simplicial $\mathbb{Q}$-vector spaces consisting of (necessarily) projective $\mathbb{Q}[\mathfrak{S}_T]$-modules, it suffices to prove that $(F_k/F_{k-1})\kappa^I_{T/}$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

For this, notice that $\mathrm{ERan}_\bullet(X,I)_{T/}$ computes the relative homology of the pair of simplicial sets $\left(F_k\mathrm{ERan}_\bullet(X)_{T/},F_{k-1}\mathrm{ERan}_\bullet(X)_{T/}\right)$ with \emph{constant} coefficients in $I^{\otimes T}$, and similarly 
$\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X,I)_{T/}$ computes the relative homology of the pair of simplicial sets $\left(F_k\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X)_{T/},F_{k-1}\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X)_{T/}\right)$ with constant coefficients in $I^{\otimes T}$. It suffices therefore to show that the map of simplicial sets $\kappa_{T/}\colon\mathrm{ERan}_\bullet(X)_{T/}\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Sing}^\mathrm{FS}_\bullet(X)_{T/}$ lifting $\kappa$ is a filtered weak equivalence with respect to the two-step filtration given above. This follows by applying
\cite[Corollary A.9.4]{HA} to the space $X^T$, filtered by its diagonals corresponding to all partitions of $T$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- defn-14: body_md -->
\label{defn:cAheart}
We let $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)$ denote the subalgebra of $\mathfrak{S}_l$-invariants
\[
\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)\coloneqq \mathrm{grad}_F\mathbb{Q}[\mathfrak{S}_l]^{\mathfrak{S}_l}\in\mathrm{Alg}(\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}^\mathbb{N}).
\]
Its part of grading $0$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Q}$; we let $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)_+\subseteq\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)$ denote the part of strictly positive grading.
<!-- end defn-14 -->
<!-- nota-11: body_md -->
\label{nota:bK}
Let $k\ge1$, let $\mu\vdash l$, and let $\underline{\lambda}=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k)$ be a sequence of partitions $\lambda_i\vdash l$. 
For $\sigma\in\mu$ we denote by $\mathbf{K}(\sigma,\underline{\lambda})$ the set of all sequences $\underline{\tau}=(\tau_1,\dots,\tau_k)$ of permutations $\tau_i\in\lambda_i$ such that the equality $\sigma=\tau_1\dots\tau_k\in\mathfrak{S}_l$ holds.
We denote by $\#\mathbf{K}(\mu,\underline{\lambda})\coloneqq\#\mathbf{K}(\sigma,\underline{\lambda})$ for any $\sigma\in\mu$.
<!-- end nota-11 -->
<!-- defn-15: body_md -->
\label{defn:cA}
We define $\mathcal{A}(l)\in\mathrm{Alg}(\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}^\mathbb{N})$ as
\[
\mathcal{A}(l)\coloneqq\mathrm{grad}_F\mathbb{Q}[\mathfrak{S}_l]_N^{\mathfrak{S}_l}\in\mathrm{Alg}(\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}^\mathbb{N}).
\]
<!-- end defn-15 -->
<!-- rem-16: body_md -->
\label{rem:evenshift}
We observe that $\mathcal{A}(l)$ may be obtained from $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)$ also in a direct, categorical way. The category $\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}^\mathbb{N}$ is endowed with a symmetric monoidal shift endofunctor $\mathrm{sh}\colon\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}^\mathbb{N}\to\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}^\mathbb{N}$, sending the sequence of spectra $(\omega_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ to the sequence $(\omega_n\ [-2n])_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$. We then have that the commutative algebra $\mathcal{A}(l)$ is the image of the commutative algebra $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)$ along $\mathrm{sh}$. Since $\mathrm{sh}$ is an equivalence, it preserves colimits; being symmetric monoidal, it also preserves factorisation homologies. In particular, for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and naturally in a space $X$ we have an equivalence of rational spectra 
\[
\left(\int_{|X|}\mathcal{A}(l)\right)_n\simeq\left(\int_{|X|}\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)\right)_n\ [-2n].
\]
<!-- end rem-16 -->
<!-- defn-16: body_md -->
\label{defn:brv}
We let $\mathbf{brv}\colon\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}\to\mathrm{Ran}_{\le2\upsilon}(\Sigma)\subseteq\mathrm{Ran}(\Sigma)$ denote the continuous map sending an isomorphism class of maps $\theta\colon C\to \Sigma$ to its set of branch values in $\Sigma$. For $1\le k\le2\upsilon$ we let $F_k\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}=\mathbf{brv}^{-1}(\mathrm{Ran}_{\le k}(\Sigma))$; this defines a filtration of $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$ by the poset $\mathbb{N}$.

We define a similar filtration of $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$ by the subspaces 
\[
F_k\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}\coloneqq F_k\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}\cup\left\{\infty\right\},
\]
and for $k=-1,-2$ we also let $F_{-1}\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}=\left\{\infty\right\}$ and $F_{-2}\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}=\emptyset$.
<!-- end defn-16 -->
<!-- lem-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:onelift}
Let $p,k\ge1$, let $s\colon\mathring{\Delta}^p\to (F_k\setminus F_{k-1})\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$ be a continuous map defined on the interior of $\Delta^p$, and assume that the composite $\mathbf{brv}\circ s$ extends to a map $\Delta^p\to\mathrm{Ran}_{\le2\upsilon}(\Sigma)$. Then $s$ extends to a continuous map $\Delta^p\to\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$.
<!-- end lem-2 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Let $(x_i)_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of points in $\mathring{\Delta}^p$ with limit $x_\infty\in\partial\Delta^p$. Let $\mathbf{brv}\circ s(x_\infty)=\left\{z_1,\dots,z_h\right\}\subseteq\Sigma$, with $h\le k$. Let $\underline{U}=(U_1,\dots,U_h)$ be disjoint open discs in $\Sigma$ with $z_j\in U_j$. Up to discarding finitely many points $x_i$, we may assume that for all $i\in\mathbb{N}$ we have $\mathbf{brv}\circ s(x)\subseteq \underline{U}$ for any $x$ lying in the straight interval joining $x_i$ with $x_{i+1}$ in $\mathring{\Delta}^p$. Pick representatives $\theta_i\colon C_i\to \Sigma$ of $s(x_i)$; by the previous we have that each $l$-fold branched cover $\theta_i$ restricts to an \'etale cover $\theta_i\colon\theta_i^{-1}(\Sigma\setminus\underline{U})\to\Sigma\setminus\underline{U}$, and that these restricted covers are pairwise isomorphic. In particular, for all $1\le j\le h$, the norm of the monodromy of $\theta_i$ around the boundary of $U_j$ only depends on $j$, but not on $i$: let us denote this number by $n_j$. There are now two cases:
\begin{itemize}
\item if $\sum_{j=1}^hn_j=2\upsilon$, then the sequence $s(x_i)$ admits a limit in $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$, given by the unique isomorphism class of covers $\theta_\infty\colon C_\infty\to\Sigma$ satisfying both of the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item the image of $\theta_\infty$ along $\mathbf{brv}$ is $\left\{z_1,\dots,z_h\right\}$;
\item the restriction of $\theta_\infty$ over $\Sigma\setminus\underline{U}$ is isomorphic to any restriction of $\theta_i$ over $\Sigma\setminus\underline{U}$;
\end{itemize}
\item if instead $\sum_{j=1}^hn_j<2\upsilon$, then the sequence $s(x_i)$ tends to $\infty$.
\end{itemize}
In all cases we have found a  limit in $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- defn-17: body_md -->
\label{defn:bL}
Let $\underline{\lambda}=(\lambda_{j,i})_{1\le j\le h,1\le i\le k_j}$ be a sequence of partitions of $l$, and assume $\sum_{i=1}^{k_j}N(\lambda_{j,i})=N(\sigma_j)$. We denote by
$\mathbf{L}(\theta_1,\underline{U},\underline{\lambda})$
the set of all isomorphism classes of pairs $(\theta_0,\psi)$ consisting of a map $\theta_0\colon C_0\to \Sigma$ of degree $l$ with source of genus $g$, branched over $P'=s(0)$, and an identification $\psi\colon\theta_0^{-1}(\Sigma\setminus\underline{U})\cong\theta_1^{-1}(\Sigma\setminus\underline{U})$ over $\Sigma\setminus\underline{U}$; we further require that the local monodromy of $\theta_0$ at $z'_{i,j}$ is in $\lambda_{i,j}$. Notice that two such pairs $(\theta_0,\psi)$ and $(\theta'_0,\psi')$, if they are isomorphic, are uniquely isomorphic. The group $\mathrm{Aut}(\theta_1)$ of automorphisms of $\theta_1\colon C_1\to \Sigma$ can be identified with the group of automorphisms of the restricted, \'etale cover $\theta_1^{-1}(\Sigma\setminus\underline{U})\to\Sigma\setminus\underline{U}$, so it acts on the set $\mathbf{L}(\theta_1,\underline{U},\underline{\lambda})$ by postcomposition on $\psi$.
<!-- end defn-17 -->
<!-- lem-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:eulerchar}
The set $\mathrm{lift}(s,\theta_1)$ of lifts of $s$ along $\mathbf{brv}$ ending at $\theta_1$ is in bijection with the set of orbits $\mathbf{L}(\theta_1,\underline{U},\underline{\lambda})/\mathrm{Aut}(\theta_1)$. Moreover, the following equality holds
\[
\sum_{t\in\mathrm{lift}(s,\theta_1)}\frac{1}{\#\mathrm{Aut}(\alpha(t))}=\frac{\#\mathbf{L}(\theta_1,\underline{U},\underline{\lambda})}{\#\mathrm{Aut}(\theta_1)},
\]
where $\#\mathrm{Aut}(\alpha(t))$ denotes the cardinality of the group of automorphisms of any representative$\theta_0$ of $\alpha(t)=t(0)$.
<!-- end lem-3 -->
<!-- lem-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:bLequalbK}
Recall Notation \ref{nota:bK}.
Then there is a bijection $\mathbf{L}(\theta_1,\underline{U},\underline{\lambda})=\prod_{j=1}^h\mathbf{K}(\sigma_j,\underline{\lambda}_j)$, where $\underline{\lambda}_j=(\lambda_{j,1},\dots,\lambda_{j,k_j})$. In particular we have
\[
\#\mathbf{L}(\theta_1,\underline{U},\underline{\lambda})=\#\mathbf{K}(\underline{\mu},\underline{\lambda})\coloneqq\prod_{j=1}^h\#\mathbf{K}(\mu_j,\underline{\lambda}_j)
\]
<!-- end lem-4 -->
<!-- defn-18: body_md -->
Similarly as in Definition \ref{defn:ER}, we let
\[
\mathrm{Sing}'_\bullet(\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}})\subseteq\mathrm{Sing}_\bullet(\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}})
\]
denote the simplicial subset spanned at level $p$ by those singular simplices $s\colon\Delta^p\to\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$ for which the following property holds: there exist $n_0\ge \dots\ge n_p\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge-1}$ such that for all $0\le i\le p$ and all $(0,\dots,0,t_i,\dots,t_p)\in\Delta^p$ with $t_i\neq0$ we have
\[
s(0,\dots,0,t_i,\dots,t_p)\in (F_{n_i}\setminus F_{n_i-1})\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}.
\]
We let $\mathrm{Sing}'_\bullet(\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}};\mathbb{Q})$ be the simplicial $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space obtained as the $\mathbb{Q}$-lineari\-sation of $\mathrm{Sing}'_\bullet(\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}})$.
For $k\ge-2$ we denote by 
\[
F_k\mathrm{Sing}'_\bullet\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}\subseteq\mathrm{Sing}'_\bullet\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}
\]
the subsimplicial set spanned by those simplices $s$ such that $\alpha(s)\in F_k\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$; we define a similar filtration on the $\mathbb{Q}$-linearisation.
<!-- end defn-18 -->
<!-- nota-12: body_md -->
For $k\ge0$ we let
\[
F_k\mathrm{Sing}'_\bullet(\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}},\infty;\mathbb{Q})\coloneqq (F_k/F_{-1})\mathrm{Sing}'_\bullet(\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}};\mathbb{Q})
.
\]
<!-- end nota-12 -->
<!-- nota-13: body_md -->
\label{nota:sscalambda}
Let $p\ge0$ and $s\in\mathrm{ERan}_p(\Sigma)$, and let $([\! [\lambda_z]\! ]_{z\in \alpha(s)})$ be a sequence of non-discrete partitions $\lambda_z\in\mathfrak{P}(l)_+$ indexed by the elements of the set $\alpha(s)\subseteq\Sigma$; assume that the equality $\sum_{z\in\alpha(s)}N(\lambda_z)=2\upsilon$ holds. 
With these data we associate the element
\[
(s,([\! [\lambda_z]\! ]_{z\in \alpha(s)})\coloneqq \otimes_{z\in\alpha(s)}[\! [\lambda_z]\! ]\ \in\  \mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)_+^{\otimes\alpha(s)}\subseteq\mathrm{ERan}_p(\Sigma,\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)_+)_{2\upsilon},
\]
where the last inclusion picks the summand indexed by $s$.
<!-- end nota-13 -->
<!-- defn-19: body_md -->
\label{defn:gamma}
We define $\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma$ as the map of simplicial $\mathbb{Q}$-vector spaces
\[
\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma\colon \mathrm{ERan}_\bullet(\Sigma,\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)_+)_{2\upsilon}\to \mathrm{Sing}'_\bullet(\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}},\infty;\mathbb{Q})
\]
sending the basis element $(s,([\! [\lambda_z]\! ]_{z\in \alpha(s)}))$ at level $p\ge0$ to the sum
\[
\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma(s,([\! [\lambda_z]\! ]_{z\in \alpha(s)}))\coloneqq\sum \frac{1}{\#\mathrm{Aut}(\alpha(t))}\cdot t,
\]
where $t\colon\Delta^p\to \mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$ ranges over all elements of $\mathrm{Sing}'_p(\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}})$ satisfying the following properties:
\begin{itemize}
\item the restriction $\mathring{t}\colon\mathring{\Delta}^p\hookrightarrow\Delta^p\xrightarrow{t}\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$ has image inside $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$, and the composite map $\mathbf{brv}\circ\mathring{t}$ agrees with $s$;
\item if $\theta\colon C\to\Sigma$ represents the equivalence class of $\alpha(t)$, then the local monodromy of $\theta$ at $z\in\alpha(s)\subseteq\Sigma$ belongs to the conjugacy class $\lambda_z$.
\end{itemize}
Here we denote by $\mathrm{Aut}(\alpha(t))$ the group of automorphisms of $\theta$ as above over $\Sigma$.
<!-- end defn-19 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
The filtration preserving action of $\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma)$ on the space $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$ gives rise to a filtration preserving action of the simplicial group $\mathrm{Sing}_\bullet(\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma))$ on the simplicial 
set $\mathrm{Sing}'_\bullet(\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}})$, and  after $\mathbb{Q}$-linearisation,
on the simplicial $\mathbb{Q}$-vector
space $\mathrm{Sing}'_\bullet(\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}},\infty;\mathbb{Q})$. The latter models the action of $\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma)$ on the spectrum $(|\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}|,\infty)_!\mathbb{Q}$.

Similarly, $\mathrm{Sing}_\bullet(\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma))$ acts on $\mathrm{ERan}_\bullet(\Sigma,\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)_+)_{2\upsilon}$ as follows: a $p$-simplex $t\colon\Delta^p\to\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma)$
sends the basis element $(s,([\! [\lambda_z]\! ]_{z\in \alpha(s)})))$ 
to the basis element $(t\cdot s,([\! [\lambda_{\alpha(t)^{-1}\cdot z}]\! ]_{z\in \alpha(t\cdot s)})))$.
This models the action of $\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma)$ on the spectrum $(\int_{|\Sigma|}\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l))_{2\upsilon}$. The map $\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma$ is evidently levelwise $\mathrm{Sing}_\bullet(\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma))$-equivariant.

It is left to check that $\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma$ is indeed a simplicial map, i.e. it is compatible with face and degeneracy maps in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. Fix a basis element $(s,[\! [\lambda_z]\! ]_{z\in\alpha(s)})$ of $\mathrm{ERan}_p(\Sigma,\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)_+)_{2\upsilon}$. We want to show for $1\le i\le p$ the equalities 
\[
\begin{split}
d_i\circ\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma(s,[\! [\lambda_z]\! ]_{z\in\alpha(s)})&=\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma\circ d_i(s,[\! [\lambda_z]\! ]_{z\in\alpha(s)});\\
s_i\circ\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma(s,[\! [\lambda_z]\! ]_{z\in\alpha(s)})&=\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma\circ s_i(s,[\! [\lambda_z]\! ]_{z\in\alpha(s)}).
\end{split}
\]
For all degeneracy maps and for all face maps except $d_0$, this immediately follows from Lemma \ref{lem:onelift} and the fact that $\mathbf{brv}$ is \'etale over the strata $\mathrm{Conf}_k(\Sigma)\subseteq\mathrm{Ran}(\Sigma)$. 
To check the equality involving $d_0$,
we also fix a basis element $t\in\mathrm{Sing}'_{p-1}(\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}},\infty;\mathbb{Q})$ and aim at checking that $t$ has the same coefficient on both expressions. If $\mathbf{brv}\circ t|_{\mathring{\Delta}^{p-1}}\neq d_0(s)_{\mathring{\Delta}^{p-1}}$, both coefficients of $t$ are equal because they both trivially vanish, so let us assume that the last equality holds;
by Lemma \ref{lem:onelift}
we then also have $\mathbf{brv}(\alpha(t))= \alpha(d_0((s)))$.  We let $P'=\alpha(s)$ and $P=\alpha(d_0(s))$, and expand $P=\left\{z_1,\dots,z_h\right\}$.
The restriction of $s$ along the straight segment in $\Delta^p$ joining $(1,0,\dots0)$ and $(0,1,0,\dots,0)$ gives rise to a map $P'\to P$; we let $P'_j$ be the preimage of $z_j$ along this map.
Let $\lambda_{j,i}$ be the partition $\lambda_{z_{j,i}}$, and denote by $\underline{\lambda}$ the list of all partitions $\lambda_{j,i}$. Finally, let $\mu_j\vdash l$ denote the conjugacy class of the local monodromy at $z_j\in P$ of a representative $\theta_1\colon C_1\to\Sigma$ of $\alpha(t)$.

The definition of the product in $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)$, together with the definition of $\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma$, tells us that the coefficient of $t$ in $\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma\circ d_0(s,[\! [\underline{\lambda}]\! ])$ is equal to $\#\mathbf{K}(\underline{\mu},\underline{\lambda})/\#\mathrm{Aut}(\theta_1)$, whereas the definition of 
$\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma$ tells us that the coefficient of $t$ in 
$d_0\circ\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma(s,[\! [\underline{\lambda}]\! ])$ is equal to
$\sum_{(\theta_0,\psi)\in\mathbf{L}(\theta_1,\underline{U},\underline{\lambda})}1/\#\mathrm{Aut}(\theta_0)$, where $\underline{U}$ is a union of $h$ disjoint discs in $\Sigma$ covering $P$. Combining Lemmas \ref{lem:eulerchar} and \ref{lem:bLequalbK} we obtain that the two coefficients of $t$ are equal.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:defnTheta}
In the hypotheses of Proposition \ref{prop:defnTheta}, there is a well-defined and $\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma)$-equiva\-riant map of rational spectra
\[
\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma[-4\upsilon]\ \colon
\left(\int_{\Sigma}\mathcal{A}(l)\right)_{2\upsilon(g,l,h)}\to|\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}|_*\mathbb{Q}.
\]
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
By Corollary \ref{cor:Braorbifold} and Remark \ref{rem:evenshift}, the source and target of the map in the statement are $\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma)$-equivariantly equivalent to the source and target of the map $\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma$ from Proposition \ref{prop:defnTheta}, shifted by $-4\upsilon$.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- nota-14: body_md -->
\label{nota:intfp}
For $h\ge0$ and $l\ge2$ we denote by 
\[
\int_{|\mathfrak{p}_h^{\mathrm{top}}|}\mathcal{A}(l)\in(\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}^\mathbb{N})^{|\mathfrak{M}_h^{\mathrm{top}}|}
\]
the graded parametrised rational spectrum over $|\mathfrak{M}_h^{\mathrm{top}}|\simeq\mathbf{B}\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma)$ corresponding to $\int_{|\Sigma|}\mathcal{A}(l)$ with its $\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma)$-action. Here $\Sigma$ is a closed connected topological surface of genus $h$. For $e\ge1$ we further denote
\[
\int_{|\mathfrak{p}_{h,e}|}\mathcal{A}(l)\coloneqq\varepsilon_{h,e}^*\int_{\mathfrak{p}_h}\mathcal{A}(l)\in(\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}^\mathbb{N})^{|\mathcal{H}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}|}.
\]
Finally, recalling Equation \ref{eq:cHvcrs}, for $g\ge0$ we denote by 
\[
\Theta^{g,l}_{h,e}\colon\left(\int_{|\mathfrak{p}_{h,e}|}\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)\right)_{2\upsilon(g,l,h)}\to (r_{g,l,h,e}^\infty,\infty)_!\mathbb{Q}
\]
the image along $\varepsilon^*_{h,e}$ of the map of graded parametrised rational spectra over $|\mathfrak{M}_h^{\mathrm{top}}|$ corresponding to 
$\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma$.
By Corollary \ref{cor:defnTheta} we also obtain a map
\[
\Theta^{g,l}_{h,e}[-4\upsilon(g,l,h)]\colon\left(\int_{|\mathfrak{p}_{h,e}|}\mathcal{A}(l)\right)_{2\upsilon(g,l,h)}\to (r_{g,l,h,e})_*\mathbb{Q}.
\]
<!-- end nota-14 -->
<!-- rem-17: body_md -->
By \cite[Theorem 6.1]{Bianchi:Hur3}, the algebra $\pi_*(\mathcal{A}(l))$ is isomorphic to the rational cohomology ring of the space $\mathbb{B}=\mathbb{B}((\mathfrak{S}_d^{\mathrm{geo}})_+,\mathfrak{S}_d)$ used in \cite{Bianchi:Hur3} to model a ``double delooping'' of the $E_1$-monoid $\mathrm{Hur}((0,1)^2;\mathfrak{S}_d^{\mathrm{geo}})$ of Hurwitz spaces with collisions. Das--Petersen replace $\mathbb{B}$ with the underlying homotopy type of the topological stack $\mathrm{Bra}^l_{\mathbb{R}^2}$ featuring in \cite[Theorem 6.3]{DasPetersen}. 

Intuitively, $\mathrm{Bra}^l_{\mathbb{R}^2}$ parametrises degree $l$ branched covers of the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ that have no prescribed behaviour at $\infty$. With some care, it should be possible to associate with an oriented topological surface $\Sigma$ a bundle $p\colon\mathrm{Bra}^l_{T\Sigma}\to\Sigma$ of topological stacks, whose fibre at $x\in \Sigma$ is $\mathrm{Bra}^l_{T_x\Sigma}$.
There should then also be a scanning map 
\[
\mathrm{Bra}^l_\Sigma\to\Gamma(p)=\Gamma(\mathrm{Bra}^l_{T\Sigma}\xrightarrow{p}\Sigma),
\]
which loosely sends $\theta\colon C\to \Sigma$ to the section sending $x\in\Sigma$ to the part of $C$ lying over a small neighbourhood of $x$.

In this light, the map $\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma$ from Corollary \ref{cor:defnTheta} ``wants to'' be the induced on rational cochains by the previous scanning map. There are still some issues with this interpretation, and it would be interesting if one could resolve them:
\begin{itemize}
\item we are identifying $\Gamma(p)_*\mathbb{Q}$ with $\int_{|\Sigma|} p_*\mathbb{Q}$ as functors $\Sigma\to\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q})$; to do this we would need the relevant Eilenberg--Moore spectral sequence to converge, however this is not guaranteed as $\Sigma$ is 2-dimensional and the homotopy type fibre $|\mathrm{Bra}^l_{\mathbb{R}^2}|$ of $p$ is not 2-connected ;
\item we are further identifying $\int_{|\Sigma|} p_*\mathbb{Q}$ and the constant functor at $|\mathrm{Bra}^l_{\mathbb{R}^2}|_*\mathbb{Q}$ with each other, as  functors $|\Sigma|\to\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q})$; however the topological tangent bundle of $\Sigma$ is usually non-trivial;
\item we are replacing $|\mathrm{Bra}^l_{\mathbb{R}^2}|_*\mathbb{Q}$ with its cohomology algebra; this requires the fibration $|p|\colon|\mathrm{Bra}^l_{T\Sigma}|\to|\Sigma|$, with homotopy fibre $|\mathrm{Bra}^l_{\mathbb{R}^2}|$, to be rationally formal \emph{as a fibration}, something which is not clear.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end rem-17 -->
<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:Thetaisomorphism}
The composite $\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma)$-equivariant map of rational spectra
\[
\left(\int_{|\Sigma|}\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)\right)_{2\upsilon}\xrightarrow{\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma}\left(\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}},\infty\right)_!\mathbb{Q} \xrightarrow{\ddot w_\mathbb{Q}}\left(\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}},\infty\right)_!\mathbb{Q}
\]
induces an isomorphism on homotopy groups in the range of degrees
\[
*>4\upsilon-(2\upsilon-J_l)/I_l.
\]
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- defn-20: body_md -->
\label{defn:dCBra}
Let $A\subseteq B\subseteq\Sigma$ be finite subsets as in Definition \ref{defn:Bra}. We denote by $\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} A{\,\text{\'et}\,} B}\subseteq\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} A{\,\text{\'et}\,} B}$ the open topological substack spanned at $X$ by the sequences $(Y,p,\vartheta,\mathbf{t})$ satisfying for all $x\in X$ the following properties:
\begin{itemize}
\item the branched cover $\theta\colon p^{-1}(x)\to\Sigma$ admits at least one simple branch value, i.e., a point of $\Sigma$ whose associated local monodromy is a transposition;
\item the branched cover $\theta\colon p^{-1}(x)\to\Sigma$ does not factor through any intermediate branched cover.
\end{itemize}
When $A=\emptyset$, we denote by $\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{\'et}\,} B,\mathrm{crs}}$ the coarse space of $\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{\'et}\,} B}$.
<!-- end defn-20 -->
<!-- defn-21: body_md -->
\label{defn:tranmongroup}
Let $a\in\Sigma$ and let $(C,\theta,\mathbf{t})\in\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} a}$, i.e. $\theta\colon C\to\Sigma$ is an $l$-fold branched cover with connected source of genus $g$, branched at some subset $P\subseteq\Sigma\setminus \left\{a\right\}$, and $\mathbf{t}\colon\theta^{-1}(a)\cong\underline{l}$ is a trivialisation. Let $\varphi\colon\pi_1(\Sigma\setminus P,a)\to\mathfrak{S}_l$ be the monodromy group homomorphism associated with $(C,\theta,\mathbf{t})$.

The \emph{monodromy group} of $(C,\theta,\mathbf{t})$, denoted $\mathbf{MG}(C,\theta,\mathbf{t})=\mathbf{MG}(P,\varphi)$, is the subgroup of $\mathfrak{S}_l$ given by the image of $\varphi$.
If $\theta$ admits at least one simple branch value, the 
\emph{transposition monodromy group} of $(C,\theta,\mathbf{t})$, denoted $\mathbf{TMG}(C,\theta,\mathbf{t})=\mathbf{TMG}(P,\varphi)$, is the subgroup of $\mathbf{MG}(\theta,\mathbf{t})$ generated by all transpositions that arise as images along $\varphi$ of small loops based at $a$, in the sense of Definition \ref{defn:smallloop}.
<!-- end defn-21 -->
<!-- lem-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:minimalfactorisation}
Let $\theta\colon C\to\Sigma$ be a connected $l$-fold cover branched at $P\subseteq \Sigma$ and admitting at least one simple branch value. 
Then there exists an essentially unique factorisation of $\theta$ as a composite of branched covers of oriented, connected topological surfaces
$C\xrightarrow{\eta} \bar C\xrightarrow{\bar\theta}\Sigma
$
satisfying the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\eta$ has degree $>1$ and admits at least a simple branch value;
\item if $C\xrightarrow{\breve\eta} D\xrightarrow{\breve\theta}\Sigma$ is any factorisation of $\theta$ with $\breve\eta$ of degree $>1$, then $\breve\eta$ factors as a composite $C\xrightarrow{\eta}\bar C\to D$ in such a way that $\bar C\to D\xrightarrow{\breve\theta}\Sigma$ agrees with $\bar\theta$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-5 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
We consider on the space $\theta^{-1}(\Sigma\setminus P)\subseteq C$ the equivalence relation $\sim$ generated by $w\sim w'$ whenever the following hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\theta(w)=\theta(w')$; let us temporarily denote by $a$ this point;
\item there exists a small loop $\gamma\subseteq\Sigma\setminus P$, based at $a$, whose local monodromy with respect to $\theta$ is a transposition, and lifting to a path in $\theta^{-1}(\Sigma\setminus P)$ from $w$ to $w'$.
\end{itemize}
We consider $\sim$ as a subset of $\theta^{-1}(\Sigma\setminus P)^2$; the closure $\bar\sim\subseteq C^2$ is again an equivalence relation on $C$, and we let $\bar C=C/\bar\sim$, and factor $\theta$ through the quotient map $\eta\colon C\to \bar C$ followed by a further map $\bar\theta\colon \bar C\to \Sigma$. Note that $\bar C$ is again a topological surface.

The assumption on $\theta$ imples that $\sim$, and hence also $\bar\sim$, is not the trivial equivalence relation, so that $\eta$ has degree $>1$; moreover, if $z\in P$ is a simple branch value for $\theta$, then $\bar\theta$ must be \'etale over $z$ and $\eta$ must be \'etale over all points of $\bar\theta^{-1}(z)$ except one, which is a simple branch value for $\eta$. This proves (1).

To prove (2), we argue that given any factorisation $C\xrightarrow{\breve\eta} D\xrightarrow{\breve\theta} \Sigma$ of $\theta$, the equivalence relation on $C$ yielding $D$ as a quotient must be coarser than $\bar\sim$. To see this, it suffices to show that the equivalence relation on $\theta^{-1}(\Sigma\setminus P)$ yielding $\breve\theta^{-1}(\Sigma\setminus P)$ as quotient is coarser than $\sim$. To wit, let $w\sim w'$ be points in $\theta^{-1}(a)$, for some $a\in\Sigma\setminus P$, and assume that there is a simple loop $\gamma$ in $\Sigma\setminus P$ spinning around a simple branch value $z\in P$ and lifting to a path in $\theta^{-1}(\Sigma\setminus P)$ from $w$ to $w'$. Since $P$ is a simple branch value, $\breve\theta$ must be \'etale over $P$, and in particular the lift of $\gamma$ that starts at $\breve\eta(w)$ also ends at $\breve\eta(w)$. But this lift is the projection along $\breve\eta$ of the lift of $\gamma$ along $\theta$ from $w$ to $w'$, whence $\breve\eta(w)=\breve\eta(w')$.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- nota-15: body_md -->
We denote by $\mathrm{Sing}'_\bullet(\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}},\infty;\mathbb{Q})$ the quotient of the simplicial $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space $\mathrm{Sing}'_\bullet(\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}},\infty;\mathbb{Q})$ by all simplices $t\colon\Delta^p\to  \mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$ such that $\alpha(t)\notin\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$.
<!-- end nota-15 -->
<!-- nota-16: body_md -->
We define a filtration $F_\star$ on $\mathrm{Sing}'_\bullet(\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}},\infty;\mathbb{Q})$ as the image of the filtration $F_\star$ on $\mathrm{Sing}'_\bullet(\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}},\infty;\mathbb{Q})$.
<!-- end nota-16 -->
<!-- lem-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:first_reduction}
Assume that for all $1\le k\le 2\upsilon$ the map of simplicial $\mathbb{Q}$-vector spaces $(F_k/F_{k-1})(\ddot w_\mathbb{Q}\circ\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma)$ is injective on homology groups in all degrees, and an isomorphism in degrees $*>2k-(2k-2\upsilon-J_l)/I_l$. Then Theorem \ref{thm:Thetaisomorphism} holds true.
<!-- end lem-6 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
The map of filtered simplicial $\mathbb{Q}$-vector spaces $\ddot w_\mathbb{Q}\circ\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma$ gives rise to a comparison map between the spectral sequences computing the homology of the source and target of $\ddot w_\mathbb{Q}\circ\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma$. The hypothesis, together with the assumption $I_l\ge1$ from Notation \ref{nota:goodconstantsIJ}, implies that the map on $E^1$-pages is an isomorphism on $E^1_{k,*-k}$ for all $*>2k-(2k-2\upsilon-J_l)/I_l\ge4\upsilon-(2\upsilon-J_l)/I_l$ and an injection on $E^1_{k,*-k}$ for all $k,*$, whence a standard spectral sequence argument proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- defn-22: body_md -->
\label{defn:colconf}
Recall Definition \ref{defn:Ran}. Let $X$ be a space and let $S$ be a finite set.
We denote by $\mathrm{Conf}_k(X,S)$ the space of configurations of $k$ points in $X$ with labels in $S$. It is defined as the quotient
\[
\mathrm{Conf}_k(X,S)\coloneqq\left(\left\{(z_1,\dots,z_k)\in X^k\,|\,z_i\neq z_j\right\}\times S^k\right)/\mathfrak{S}_k.
\]
It is a finite \'etale cover of $\mathrm{Conf}_k(X)$.
If $S$ carries a grading $S\to\mathbb{N}$, we denote by $\mathrm{Conf}_k(X,S)_n$ the subspace of configurations whose sum of labels is equal to $n$.
If $\underline{k}=(k_s)_{s\in S}$ is a sequence of natural numbers with $k=\sum_{s\in S}k_s$,
we let $\mathrm{Conf}_{\underline{k}}(X)$ denote the $\underline{k}$-coloured configuration space of $X$, i.e. the subspace of $\mathrm{Conf}_k(X,S)$ containing configurations in which precisely $k_s$ points carry the label $s\in S$.
<!-- end defn-22 -->
<!-- nota-17: body_md -->
Recall Notation \ref{nota:fP}. We consider on $\mathfrak{P}(l)_+$ the grading $N\colon\mathfrak{P}(l)_+\to\mathbb{N}$ as in Definition \ref{defn:norm}
<!-- end nota-17 -->
<!-- nota-18: body_md -->
\label{nota:Xi}
We denote by $\Xi_k$ the set of all sequences $\underline{k}=(k_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\mathfrak{P}(l)_+}$ of natural numbers with $\sum_{\lambda\in\mathfrak{P}(l)_+}k_\lambda=k$ and $\sum_{\lambda\in\mathfrak{P}(l)_+}k_\lambda\cdot N(\lambda)=2\upsilon$. The set $\Xi_k$ is in natural bijection with $\pi_0(\mathrm{Conf}_k(\Sigma,\mathfrak{P}(l)_+)_{2\upsilon})$.
<!-- end nota-18 -->
<!-- lem-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:second_reduction}
Assume that for all $1\le k\le2\upsilon$ the restricted \'etale map
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:tbrvrestricted}
\widetilde{\mathbf{brv}}\colon(F_k\setminus F_{k-1})\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}\to\mathrm{Conf}_k(\Sigma,\mathfrak{P}(l)_+)_{2\upsilon}
\end{equation}
induces an isomorphism in rational cohomology in the range of cohomological degrees $*<(2k-2\upsilon-J_l)/I_l$. Then the assumptions of Lemma \ref{lem:first_reduction} hold true.
<!-- end lem-7 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
We may identify $(F_k/F_{k-1})\mathrm{Sing}'_\bullet(\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}},\infty;\mathbb{Q})$ with the simplicial $\mathbb{Q}$-vector subspace of $\mathrm{Sing}_\bullet\left(\left((F_k\setminus F_{k-1})\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}\right)^\infty,\infty;\mathbb{Q}\right)$ spanned by simplices $s\colon\Delta^p\to\left((F_k\setminus F_{k-1})\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}\right)^\infty$ such that $s^{-1}(\infty)$ is a terminal subsimplex of $\Delta^p$. A similar remark holds for $\left((F_k\setminus F_{k-1})\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}\right)^\infty$. By
\cite[Corollary A.9.4]{HA}, the map $(F_k/F_{k-1})\ddot w_\mathbb{Q}$ models the collapse map
\[
\left(\left((F_k\setminus F_{k-1})\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}\right)^\infty,\infty\right)_!\mathbb{Q}\to\left(\left((F_k\setminus F_{k-1})\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}\right)^\infty,\infty\right)_!\mathbb{Q}
\]
which under Poincar\'e--Lefschetz duality corresponds to the shifted restriction map along the open inclusion
\[
\left((F_k\setminus F_{k-1})\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}\right)_*\mathbb{Q}[2k]\to\left((F_k\setminus F_{k-1})\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}\right)_*\mathbb{Q}[2k].
\]

Similarly, $(F_k/F_{k-1})\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma$ models a ``weighted'' version of the shifted restriction map along the finite \'etale cover $\widetilde{\mathbf{brv}}$
\[
\left(\mathrm{Conf}_k(\Sigma,\mathfrak{P}(l)_+)_{2\upsilon}\right)_*\mathbb{Q}\to\left((F_k\setminus F_{k-1})\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}\right)_*\mathbb{Q},
\]
described precisely as follows. Let $Z\subseteq (F_k\setminus F_{k-1})\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$ be a connected component, and let $\mathrm{Conf}_{\underline{k}}(\Sigma)=\widetilde{\mathbf{brv}}(Z)$. Observe that if $\theta\colon C\to\Sigma$ and $\theta'\colon C'\to\Sigma$ represent classes in $Z$, then there is a homeomorphism $C\cong C'$ covering a homeomorphism $\Sigma\cong\Sigma$; in particular the number $n=\#\mathrm{Aut}(\theta)\ge1$ is also equal to $\#\mathrm{Aut}(\theta')$, i.e. it only depends on $Z$. Then $\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma$ restricts to a simplicial map
\[
\mathrm{ERan}_\bullet(\Sigma,\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)_+)_{\underline{k}}\to\mathrm{Sing}'_\bullet(Z^\infty,\infty;\mathbb{Q})\subseteq\mathrm{Sing}'_\bullet(\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l,\infty}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}},\infty;\mathbb{Q})
\]
which models a map of rational spectra
\[
\left(\mathrm{Conf}_{\underline{k}}(\Sigma)^\infty,\infty\right)_!\mathbb{Q}\to (Z^\infty,\infty)_!\mathbb{Q},
\]
and under Poincar\'e--Lefschetz duality corresponds to the map
\[
\mathrm{Conf}_{\underline{k}}(\Sigma)_*\mathbb{Q}[2k]\to Z_*\mathbb{Q}[2k]
\]
given by $1/n$ times restriction along $\widetilde{\mathbf{brv}}$; note that the number $n$ depends on $Z$.

It follows that $(F_k/F_{k-1})(\ddot w_\mathbb{Q}\circ\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma)$ may be identified with a mild variation of the restriction map associated with \eqref{eq:tbrvrestricted}, in which we multiply by different invertible rational numbers on different components of $(F_k\setminus F_{k-1})\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$. Being a finite \'etale cover, \eqref{eq:tbrvrestricted} induces injections in rational cohomology groups. Assuming \eqref{eq:tbrvrestricted} induces an isomorphism in the range from the statement, Poincar\'e--Lefschetz duality yields the corresponding isomorphism range for $(F_k/F_{k-1})(\ddot w_\mathbb{Q}\circ\Theta^{g,l}_\Sigma)$ in homology.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- nota-19: body_md -->
For finite subsets $A\subseteq B\subseteq\Sigma$ as in Definition \ref{defn:Bra} and for $k\ge0$ we denote by $F_k\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} A{\,\text{\'et}\,} B,\mathrm{crs}}$ the preimage of $F_k\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$ along the map $\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} A{\,\text{\'et}\,} B,\mathrm{crs}}\to\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma,\mathrm{crs}}$ forgetting trivialisations over $A$ and the \'etale property over $B$.
For simplicity, we denote by
$\widetilde{\mathbf{brv}}$ also the composite map
\[
(F_k\setminus F_{k-1})\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} A{\,\text{\'et}\,} B,\mathrm{crs}}\to(F_k\setminus F_{k-1})\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{\'et}\,} B,\mathrm{crs}}\xrightarrow{\widetilde{\mathbf{brv}}}\mathrm{Conf}_k(\Sigma\setminus B,\mathfrak{P}(l)_+)_{2\upsilon}.
\]
<!-- end nota-19 -->
<!-- lem-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:third_reduction}
Assume that the restricted finite \'etale map
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:tbrv_generalised_dBra}
\widetilde{\mathbf{brv}}\colon(F_k\setminus F_{k-1}) \ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} a{\,\text{\'et}\,} B,\mathrm{crs}}\to\mathrm{Conf}_k(\Sigma\setminus B,\mathfrak{P}(l)_+)_{2\upsilon}
\end{equation}
induces an isomorphism in rational cohomology in the range of cohomological degrees $*<(2k-2\upsilon-J_l)/I_l$ for any non-empty finite subset $B\subseteq\Sigma$ and any $a\in\Sigma$. Then the assumptions of Lemma \ref{lem:second_reduction} hold true.
<!-- end lem-8 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
Let $\hat B\subseteq \Sigma$ be a subset of cardinality $2\upsilon+1$. For any non-empty subset $B\subseteq \hat B$ we may restrict \eqref{eq:tbrvrestricted} to a finite \'etale map
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:tbrvrestricted_etale_B_nonempty}
\widetilde{\mathbf{brv}}\colon(F_k\setminus F_{k-1})\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{\'et}\,} B,\mathrm{crs}}\to\mathrm{Conf}_k(\Sigma\setminus B,\mathfrak{P}(l)_+)_{2\upsilon}
\end{equation}
The sources and targets of \eqref{eq:tbrvrestricted_etale_B_nonempty} for varying $\emptyset\neq B\subseteq \hat B$ form a hypercover of the source and target of \eqref{eq:tbrvrestricted}, so that by a standard Mayer--Vietoris spectral sequence argument it suffices to show that \eqref{eq:tbrvrestricted_etale_B_nonempty} induces isomorphisms in rational cohomology in degrees $*<(2k-2\upsilon-J_l)/I_l$. For this, we may pick $a\in B$ and consider the composite 
\[
(F_k\setminus F_{k-1})\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} a{\,\text{\'et}\,} B}\to (F_k\setminus F_{k-1})\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{\'et}\,} B,\mathrm{crs}}\xrightarrow{\eqref{eq:tbrvrestricted_etale_B_nonempty}}\mathrm{Conf}_k(\Sigma\setminus B,\mathfrak{P}(l)_+)_{2\upsilon};
\]
by assumption the previous composite induces a rational cohomology isomorphism in degrees $*<(2k-2\upsilon-J_l)/I_l$, but we also know that both maps, being finite \'etale, induce injective morphisms in rational cohomology in all degrees.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- ex-4: body_md -->
\label{ex:mainsetting}
Our applications will be with $G=\mathfrak{S}_l$, $c\subseteq \mathfrak{S}_l\setminus\left\{\mathbbl{1}\right\}$ being a conjugation-invariant subset containing all transpositions, and $c_1$ being the conjugacy class of transpositions.
<!-- end ex-4 -->
<!-- nota-20: body_md -->
\label{nota:standardgenerators}
We fix a sequence $\bar P_\infty=\left\{\bar z_i\,|\,i\in\mathbb{N}\right\}$ of distinct points in $\mathring{\mathcal{F}}$ that converges to $*\in\partial_0\mathcal{F}$, and let $\bar P_k\coloneqq\left\{\bar z_1,\dots,\bar z_k\right\}$ be our preferred basepoint of $\mathrm{Conf}_k(\mathring{\mathcal{F}})$. For $k=0$ we also set $\bar P_0=\emptyset$ for uniform notation.

Further, we fix for all $k\ge0$ a system of simple loops, all disjoint from $\bar P_\infty$
\[
\alpha_1,\beta_1,\dots,\alpha_h,\beta_h,\delta_0,\dots,\delta_n,\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3,\dots\in\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P_\infty,*)
\]
as in Figure \ref{fig:loopscF},
so that in particular, for all $k\ge1$, $\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P_k,*)$ is freely generated by
the loops $\alpha_1,\beta_1,\dots,\alpha_h,\beta_h,\delta_0,\dots,\delta_n,\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_k$.
