The loop
$\delta_0$ is the \emph{counterclockwise} boundary loop around $\partial_0\mathcal{F}$, and satisfies the equality
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:delta0formula}    
\delta_0=\gamma_1\dots\gamma_k[\alpha_1,\beta_1]\dots[\alpha_h,\beta_h]\delta_1\dots\delta_n\in\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P_k,*),
\end{equation}
where $[\alpha_i,\beta_i]=\alpha_i\beta_i\alpha_i^{-1}\beta_i^{-1}$. We sometimes consider $\pi_1(\mathcal{F},*)$ as the subgroup of $\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P_k,*)$ generated by the elements $\alpha_1,\beta_1,\dots,\alpha_h,\beta_h,\delta_0,\dots,\delta_n$.

Finally, for each $k\ge1$ we fix a disc $V_k$ whose closure $\bar V_k$ is contained in $\mathring{\mathcal{F}}$, and such that $\bar P_\infty\cap V_k=\bar P_\infty\cap\bar V_k=\bar P_k$. We also fix a path $\zeta_k$ joining $*$ with $\partial V_k$ and otherwise disjoint from $V_k\cup\bar P_\infty$. We assume that the concatenation $\zeta_k\star\partial V_k\star\zeta_k^{-1}$ is homotopic, as a based loop in $\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P_\infty$, to the product $\gamma_1\dots\gamma_k$.
<!-- end nota-20 -->
<!-- nota-21: body_md -->
\label{nota:braidgroup}
We denote by $B_k^\mathcal{F}=\pi_1\left(\mathrm{Conf}_k(\mathring{\mathcal{F}}),\bar P_k\right)$ the $k$\textsuperscript{th} braid group of $\mathcal{F}$. It is endowed with a point-pushing map $B_k^\mathcal{F}\hookrightarrow\pi_0(\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P_k,\partial\mathcal{F}))$. For $1\le m\le k$ we identify the standard braid group $B_m$ with the subgroup of the image of the point-pushing map spanned by homotopy classes of homeomorphisms supported on $V_m\setminus \bar P_m$, i.e. restricting to the identity outside $V_m\setminus\bar P_m$.
<!-- end nota-21 -->
<!-- defn-23: body_md -->
\label{defn:CHur}
We let $\mathrm{Hom}^c(\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P_k,*),G)\subseteq \mathrm{Hom}(\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P_k,*),G)$ denote the subset of those group homomorphisms $\varphi$ whose evaluation at each loop $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_k$ belongs to $c$.
We let $\mathrm{Hur}^{G,c}_k(\mathcal{F})$ denote the finite \'etale cover of $\mathrm{Conf}_k(\mathring{\mathcal{F}})$ corresponding to the action of $B_k^\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathrm{Hom}^c(\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P_k,*),G)$ induced by the point-pushing map. Concretely, $\mathrm{Hur}^{G,c}_k(\mathcal{F})$ contains pairs $(P,\varphi)$ consisting of a configuration $P\in\mathrm{Conf}_k(\mathring{\mathcal{F}})$ and a group homomorphism $\varphi\colon\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus P,*)\to G$ whose evaluation at any small loop spinning clockwise around a point of $P$ belongs to $c$.

We let $\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hom}^c(\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P_k,*),G)$ denote the subset of surjective group homomorphism; it is $B^\mathcal{F}_k$-invariant, and we let $\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hur}_k^{G,c}(\mathcal{F})\subseteq\mathrm{Hur}^{G,c}_k(\mathcal{F})$ denote the corresponding subspace.

If $\underline{k}=(k_1,\dots,k_v)$ is a sequence of natural numbers with $k=\sum_{i=1}^vk_i$, and  $\underline{\nu}=(\nu_1,\dots,\nu_n)$ is a sequence of conjugacy classes in $G$ (possibly different than those contained in $c$), and $\omega\in G$ is any element, we let $\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hom}^c_{\underline{k},\underline{\nu},\omega}(\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P_k,*),G)\subseteq\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hom}^c(\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P_k,*),G)$ denote the subset of group homomorphisms $\varphi$ such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item there are precisely $k_i$ values of $1\le j\le k$ for which $\varphi(\gamma_j)\in c_j$;
\item $\varphi(\delta_i)\in\nu_i$, and $\varphi(\delta_0)=\omega$.
\end{itemize}
It is a $B^\mathcal{F}_k$-invariant subset, and we let $\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hur}^{G,c}_{\underline{k},\underline{\nu},\omega}(\mathcal{F})\subseteq\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hur}^{G,c}_k(\mathcal{F})$ denote the corresponding subspace. For reasons that will become clear in Example \ref{ex:tbrvexplained}, we also denote by $\widetilde{\mathbf{brv}}\colon\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hur}^{G,c}_{\underline{k},\underline{\nu},\omega}(\mathcal{F})\to\mathrm{Conf}_{\underline{k}}(\mathring{\mathcal{F}})$ the covering map sending $(P,\varphi)$ to the set $P$, each of whose points is coloured by the conjugacy class of its local monodromy with respect to $\varphi$.
<!-- end defn-23 -->
<!-- ex-5: body_md -->
\label{ex:tbrvexplained}
Let $B=\left\{a,b_1,\dots,b_n\right\}\subseteq \Sigma$ be a finite subset of cardinality $n+1$, and fix disjoint open discs $\underline{U}=(U_0,\dots, U_n)$ in $\Sigma$, with $a\in U_0$ and $b_i\in U_i$. Let $\mathcal{F}=\Sigma\setminus\underline{U}$, and let $*\in\partial_0\mathcal{F}$ be any point.

Consider the setting of Example \ref{ex:mainsetting}, and 
let $\underline{k}\in\Xi_k$ as in Notation \ref{nota:Xi}, with the number $k_{\mathrm{trsp}}$ associated with the conjugacy class of transpositions being strictly positive. 
Let $\underline{\nu}=\underline{\mathbbl{1}}$ be the sequence repeating $n$ times the conjugacy class of $\mathbbl{1}\in\mathfrak{S}_l$, and let also $\omega=\mathbbl{1}\in\mathfrak{S}_l$. 
Then there is a commutative diagram as follows, in which the horizontal arrows are both open inclusions and weak equivalences:
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hur}^{\mathfrak{S}_l,c}_{\underline{k},\underline{\mathbbl{1}},\mathbbl{1}}(\mathcal{F})\ar[d,"\widetilde{\mathbf{brv}}"]\ar[r,hook,"\simeq"]&((F_k\setminus F_{k-1})\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} a{\,\text{\'et}\,} B})_{\underline{k}}\ar[d,"\widetilde{\mathbf{brv}}"]\\
\mathrm{Conf}_{\underline{k}}(\mathring{\mathcal{F}})\ar[r,hook,"\simeq"]&\mathrm{Conf}_{\underline{k}}(\Sigma\setminus B).
\end{tikzcd}
\]
Here, the top inclusion sends a pair $(P,\varphi)$ to the essentially unique triple $(C,\theta,\mathbf{t})$
such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\theta\colon C\to\Sigma$ is \'etale over the closure of $\underline{U}$, and in particular we may extend $\mathbf{t}$ to a trivialisation of $\theta$ over $U_0$;
\item the restriction of $\theta$ over $\mathcal{F}$, with the given trivialisation over $*\in\partial_0\mathcal{F}$, is isomorphic to the $l$-fold branched cover trivialised over $*$ associated with $(P,\varphi)$.
\end{itemize}
The fact that the top map lands inside $\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} a{\,\text{\'et}\,} B}\subseteq\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} a{\,\text{\'et}\,} B}$ is a consequence of the discussion from Subsection \ref{subsec:TMG} and the assumption $k_{\mathrm{trsp}}\ge1$. Lemma \ref{lem:third_reduction} invites us to study the cohomology behaviour of the right vertical map, but we may henceforth focus on the left vertical map instead, at least to deal with those $\underline{k}\in\Xi_k$ satisfying $k_{\mathrm{trsp}}\ge1$. If $k_\mathrm{trsp}=0$, the top right space is empty, according to the definition of $\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_{\Sigma{\,\text{rel}\,} a{\,\text{\'et}\,} B}$ that we gave, and we have no such square.
<!-- end ex-5 -->
<!-- nota-22: body_md -->
\label{nota:uphi}
We represent a group homomorphism $\varphi\colon\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P_k,*)\to G$ by the list $\underline{\varphi}\coloneqq(\varphi(\gamma_1),\dots,\varphi(\gamma_k),\varphi(\alpha_1),\varphi(\beta_1),\dots,\varphi(\alpha_h),\varphi(\beta_h),\varphi(\delta_1),\dots,\varphi(\delta_n)
)$ of its values at the generators from Notation \ref{nota:standardgenerators}, taken in this order. We say that $\underline{\varphi}$ is \emph{standard} if there is $0\le r\le k$ such that $\varphi(\gamma_i)\in c_1$ if and only if $i\le r$.
<!-- end nota-22 -->
<!-- nota-23: body_md -->
For $1\le m\le k$ and $\gamma\in\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus(\bar P_k\setminus \bar P_m),*)$ we denote by $\mathfrak{b}_m(\gamma)\in B_k^\mathcal{F}$ any braid corresponding to a homeomorphism $\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P_k\to\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P_k$ obtained by dragging $V_k\setminus\bar P_k$ along $\gamma$. Here we use the paths $\zeta_k$ from Notation \ref{nota:standardgenerators} to let a based loop at $*$ drag $V_k$; the resulting element in $B_k^\mathcal{F}$ is uniquely determined up to right multiplication by an element in the subgroup $B_m\subseteq B_k^\mathcal{F}$. In particular, $\mathfrak{b}_1(\gamma)$ is uniquely determined.
<!-- end nota-23 -->
<!-- lem-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:braidactionrules}
Let $\underline{\varphi}$ be as in Notation \ref{nota:uphi}, and fix $1\le m\le k$ such that there is $\mathfrak{g}\in G$ with $\varphi(\gamma_1)=\dots=\varphi(\gamma_m)=\mathfrak{g}$. Then the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item Suppose first that $\mathfrak{g}^m=\mathbbl{1}\in G$, let $\gamma\in\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus(\bar P_k\setminus \bar P_m),*)$, and let $\tilde\gamma$ be any lift of $\gamma$ to $\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus(V_m\cup\bar P_k))$; then $\mathfrak{b}_m(\gamma)$ sends $\underline{\varphi}$ to the sequence obtained from $\underline{\varphi}$ by replacing the first $m$ entries, all equal to $\mathfrak{g}$, with $m$ entries all equal to $\varphi(\tilde\gamma)\mathfrak{g}\varphi(\tilde\gamma)^{-1}$; this is in particular independent of the choice of $\mathfrak{b}_m(\gamma)$, since $\underline{\varphi}$ is fixed by the action of $B_m$;
\item Now suppose $m=1$; then, for the following values of $\gamma$, the image  $\underline{\varphi}'$ of $\underline{\varphi}$ along $\mathfrak{b}_1(\gamma)$ satisfies the corresponding properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item{\bf $\gamma=\gamma_i$ for some $2\le i\le k$:} we have $\varphi'(\gamma_i)=\mathfrak{g}\varphi(\gamma_i)\mathfrak{g}^{-1}$, and $\underline{\varphi}'$ coincides with $\underline{\varphi}$ in all subsequent positions;
\item{\bf $\gamma=\alpha_i$ for some $1\le i \le h$:} we have $\varphi'(\alpha_i)=\mathfrak{g}\varphi(\alpha_i)\mathfrak{g}^{-1}$, $\varphi'(\beta_i)=\varphi(\beta_i)\mathfrak{g}^{-1}$, and $\underline{\varphi}'$ coincides with $\underline{\varphi}$ in all subsequent positions;
\item{\bf $\gamma=\alpha_i\beta_i\alpha_i^{-1}$ for some $1\le i \le h$:} we have $\varphi'(\alpha_i)=\mathfrak{g}\varphi(\alpha_i)$, $\varphi'(\beta_i)=\varphi(\beta_i)$, and $\underline{\varphi}'$ coincides with $\underline{\varphi}$ in all subsequent positions;
\item{\bf $\gamma=\delta_i$ for some $1\le i\le n$:} we have $\varphi'(\delta_i)=\mathfrak{g}\varphi(\delta_i)\mathfrak{g}^{-1}$, and $\underline{\varphi}'$ coincides with $\underline{\varphi}$ in all subsequent positions.
\end{enumerate}
\end{itemize}
<!-- end lem-9 -->
<!-- nota-24: body_md -->
\label{nota:fj}
We abbreviate by $\mathfrak{o}\ge1$ the order of an element in $c_1\subseteq G$, and we let $\mathfrak{j}$ be the minimal number $r\ge1$ satisfying  the following property:
for any $(\mathfrak{g}_1,\dots,\mathfrak{g}_r)\in c_1^r$ there exists an element of the standard braid group $B_r$ whose image $(\mathfrak{g}'_1,\dots,\mathfrak{g}'_r)$ satisfies the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\mathfrak{g}'_1=\dots=\mathfrak{g}'_{\mathfrak{o}}$;
\item the subgroup of $G$ generated by $\mathfrak{g}'_{\mathfrak{o}+1},\dots,\mathfrak{g}'_r$ coincides with the subgroup generated by $\mathfrak{g}'_1,\dots,\mathfrak{g}'_r$.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end nota-24 -->
<!-- ex-6: body_md -->
In the setting of Example \ref{ex:mainsetting} we have $\mathfrak{o}=2$ and $\mathfrak{j}=l+1$; this can be seen for instance as a consequence of \cite[Proposition 7.13]{Bianchi:Hur1}.
<!-- end ex-6 -->
<!-- lem-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:basicreplacement}
Let $\underline{\varphi}\in\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hom}^c_{\underline{k},\underline{\nu},\omega}(\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P,*),G)$ for some $\underline{k},\underline{\nu},\omega$ as in Definition \ref{defn:CHur}. Assume that $\underline{\varphi}$ is standard in the sense of Notation \ref{nota:uphi}. Assume $k_1\ge\mathfrak{j}$. For $1\le i\le n$ fix elements $\mathfrak{g}_i\in\nu_i$, and for $\mathfrak{j}+1\le i\le k$ fix elements $\mathfrak{g}'_i$ conjugate to $\varphi(\gamma_i)$. Then there is a braid in $B_k^\mathcal{F}$ sending $\underline{\varphi}$ to a sequence $\underline{\varphi}'$ satisfying $\varphi'(\gamma_i)=\mathfrak{g}'_i$ for $i\ge \mathfrak{j}+1$, $\varphi'(\alpha_i)=\varphi'(\beta_i)=\mathbbl{1}$, $\varphi'(\delta_i)=\mathfrak{g}_i$, and moreover the elements $\varphi'(\gamma_1),\dots,\varphi'(\gamma_\mathfrak{j})$ generate $G$.
<!-- end lem-10 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
We refer to the operations described in Lemma \ref{lem:braidactionrules}.
Up to a braid in $B_{\mathfrak{j}}$ we may assume $\varphi(\gamma_1)=\dots=\varphi(\gamma_\mathfrak{o})$ and that the image of $\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus(V_{\mathfrak{j}}\cup \bar P_k),*)$ along $\varphi$ is the entire $G$. For any element $\mathfrak{g}\in c_1$ we may then choose a suitable element $\gamma\in\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus(\bar P_k\setminus\bar P_{\mathfrak{o}}),*)$ such that $\mathfrak{b}_{\mathfrak{o}}(\gamma)$ sends $\underline{\varphi}$ to the sequence obtained from $\varphi$ by replacing the first $\mathfrak{o}$ entries by $\mathfrak{g}$. Assuming now $\varphi(\gamma_1)=\mathfrak{g}$, we may use operation (4) to conjugate $\varphi(\delta_i)$ by $\mathfrak{g}$, while keeping untouched the subsequent entries of $\underline{\varphi}$. Repeating the procedure several times, we may conjugate $\varphi(\delta_i)$ by any word in $c_1$, that is, by any element of $G$: we may therefore achieve $\varphi(\delta_i)=\mathfrak{g}_i$. We may repeat this process for decreasing $i$, until the equality $\varphi(\delta_i)=\mathfrak{g}_i$ holds simultaneously for all $1\le i\le n$. We next operate a similar strategy to adjust first $\varphi(\beta_i)$ using operation (2), and then $\varphi(\alpha_i)$, by operation (3); we adjust these pairs for decreasing $1\le i\le h$. Finally, we operate similarly, but via operations (1), to adjust $\varphi(\gamma_i)=\mathfrak{g}'_i$ for decreasing $\mathfrak{j}+1\le i\le k$. 

Suppose now that the subgroup $H$ generated by $\varphi(\gamma_1),\dots,\varphi(\gamma_\mathfrak{j})\in c_1$ is not the entire $G$, and let $\mathfrak{g}\in c_1\setminus H$. By a suitable braid in $B_\mathfrak{j}$ we may achieve that $\varphi(\gamma_1)=\dots=\varphi(\gamma_\mathfrak{o})$ and that $\varphi(\gamma_{\mathfrak{o}+1}),\dots,\varphi(\gamma_\mathfrak{j})$ generate $H$. By a suitable operation of the first kind from Lemma \ref{lem:braidactionrules} we may now replace the first $\mathfrak{o}$ entries of $\underline{\varphi}$ by the element $\mathfrak{g}$. After this replacement, the subgroup of $G$ generated by $\varphi(\gamma_1),\dots,\varphi(\gamma_\mathfrak{j})$ is strictly larger than $H$, in that it contains $H$ and also $\mathfrak{g}$. Repeating this procedure a suitable number of times gives the result.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- cor-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:CHurconnected}
Consider the setting of Example \ref{ex:mainsetting} and let $\underline{k},\underline{\nu},\omega$ be as in Definition \ref{defn:CHur}. Assume also that $k_\mathrm{trsp}\ge 2l-2$ and that the sum 
\[
\sum_{\lambda\subseteq c}k_\lambda\cdot N(\lambda)+\sum_{i=1}^nN(\nu_i)+N(\omega)
\]
is even. Then the space $\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hur}^{\mathfrak{S}_d,c}_{\underline{k},\underline{\nu},\omega}(\mathcal{F})$ is connected.
<!-- end cor-3 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
It suffices to prove that the set $\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hom}^{c}_{\underline{k},\underline{\nu},\omega}(\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P,*),\mathfrak{S}_l)$ is non-empty, and that it consists of a single orbit under the $B^\mathcal{F}_k$-action. For $l=2$ this set consists of a single element, so let us assume $l\ge3$ henceforth.

To find some $\underline{\varphi}\in \dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hom}^{\mathfrak{S}_l\setminus\mathbbl{1}}_{\underline{k},\underline{\nu},\omega}(\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P,*),\mathfrak{S}_l)$, we start by choosing arbitrary elements $\varphi(\delta_i)\in\nu_i$, we set for simplicity $\varphi(\alpha_i)=\varphi(\beta_i)=\mathbbl{1}$, and we also fix the elements $\varphi(\gamma_{2l-1}),\dots,\varphi(\gamma_k)$ so that the conjugacy class of transpositions occurs $k_\mathrm{trsp}-2l+2$ times, and each other $\lambda\subseteq c$ occurs $k_\lambda$ times. We may then compute the product
\[
\sigma=\omega\,\varphi\left(\gamma_{2l-1}\dots\gamma_k[\alpha_1,\beta_1]\dots[\alpha_h,\beta_h]\delta_1\dots\delta_n\right)^{-1}\in\mathfrak{S}_l,
\]
which by the assumptions is an even permutation. We may therefore write $\sigma$ as a product of $2l-2$ transpositions $\varphi(\gamma_1)\dots\varphi(\gamma_{2l-2})$, and we may even pick the first $l-1$ to be generators of $\mathfrak{S}_l$.

To see that there is a single $B^\mathcal{F}_k$-orbit, we let $\underline{\varphi},\underline{\varphi}'\in \dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hom}^{\mathfrak{S}_l\setminus\mathbbl{1}}_{\underline{k},\underline{\nu},\omega}(\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P,*),\mathfrak{S}_l)$;
up to applying a braids in $B_k$ to $\underline{\varphi}$ and $\underline{\varphi}'$, we may assume that $\varphi(\gamma_i)$ is conjugate to $\varphi'(\gamma_i)$ for all $i$, and moreover that $\varphi(\gamma_i)$ and $\varphi'(\gamma_i)$ are transpositions for $1\le i\le 2l-2$. By Lemma \ref{lem:basicreplacement}, we may apply braids in $B^\mathcal{F}_k$ to $\underline{\varphi}$ and $\underline{\varphi}'$ and further assume that they coincide past the first $\mathfrak{j}=l+1$ entries; we may moreover assume that both lists $\varphi(\gamma_1),\dots,\varphi(\gamma_{l+1})$ and $\varphi'(\gamma_1),\dots,\varphi'(\gamma_{l+1})$ generate $\mathfrak{S}_l$. Since we also have
\[
\varphi(\gamma_1\dots\gamma_{l+1})=\omega\,\varphi\left(\gamma_{l+2}\dots\gamma_k[\alpha_1,\beta_1]\dots[\alpha_h,\beta_h]\delta_1\dots\delta_n\right)^{-1}=\varphi'(\gamma_1\dots\gamma_{l+1}),
\]
by \cite[Proposition 7.11]{Bianchi:Hur1} we may find a braid in $B_{l+1}$ sending $\underline{\varphi}$ to $\underline{\varphi}'$.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- lem-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:quotientmodule}
Consider on the set $\mathrm{Hom}(\pi_1(\mathcal{F}),G)$ the equivalence relation generated by $\underline{\varphi}\sim\underline{\varphi}'$ if there exist elements $\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{g}'\in c_1$ such that the concatenations $(\mathfrak{g},\underline{\varphi}),(\mathfrak{g}',\underline{\varphi}')$, viewed as elements of $\mathrm{Hom}^c(\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P_1,*),G)$ in the light of Notation \ref{nota:uphi}, belong to the same $B_1^\mathcal{F}$-orbit. Then the equivalence classes of $\varphi$ are in natural bijection with the set of $n$-tuples $\underline{\nu}=(\nu_1,\dots,\nu_n)$ of conjugacy classes in $G$, the bijection sending $\underline{\varphi}$ to the sequence of conjugacy classes of $\varphi(\delta_i)$ for $1\le i\le n$.
<!-- end lem-11 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
It is evident that the conjugacy classes of the  $\delta_i$-entries are invariant under the equivalence relation $\sim$. Viceversa, if $\underline{\varphi}$ and $\underline{\varphi}'$ satisfy that $\varphi(\delta_i)$ is conjugate to $\varphi'(\delta_i)$ for all $1\le i\le n$, then we may use a strategy as in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:basicreplacement}: we may first conjugate $\varphi(\delta_n)$ by a sequence of elements of $c_1$, via operations of type (4), until we achieve $\varphi(\delta_n)=\varphi'(\delta_n)$. We then proceed in a similar way to gradually change $\varphi(\delta_{n-1})$ into $\varphi'(\delta_{n-1})$, and so on, until $\varphi(\delta_i)=\varphi'(\delta_i)$ for all $1\le i\le n$. We next adjust the elements $\varphi(\beta_i),\varphi(\alpha_i)$ for decreasing $1\le i\le h$. The procedure is in fact simpler than the one in Lemma \ref{lem:basicreplacement}, as we may each time directly pick any element $\mathfrak{g}\in c_1$ to concatenate with $\underline{\varphi}$, instead of producing it via an operation of the first kind described in Lemma \ref{lem:braidactionrules}.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
By Lemmas \ref{lem:first_reduction}, \ref{lem:second_reduction} and \ref{lem:third_reduction} and Example \ref{ex:tbrvexplained},  it suffices to show, for all $1\le k\le 2\upsilon$, that the map $\widetilde{\mathbf{brv}}\colon\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hur}^{\mathfrak{S}_l,\mathfrak{S}_l\setminus\mathbbl{1}}_{\underline{k},\underline{\mathbbl{1}},\mathbbl{1}}(\mathcal{F})\to\mathrm{Conf}_{\underline{k}}(\mathcal{F})$ is a rational homology isomorphism in degrees $*<(2k-2\upsilon-J_l)/I_l$, for any $\underline{k}$ in the set $\Xi_k\cong\pi_0(\mathrm{Conf}_k(\mathcal{F},\mathfrak{P}(l)_+)_{2\upsilon})$ form Notation \ref{nota:Xi}. 
If $2k-2\upsilon<J_l$ there is nothing to prove, so let us assume $2k-2\upsilon\ge J_l$ from now on. 
We next observe that if $\underline{k}\in\Xi_k$, that is, if $\sum_{\lambda\in\mathfrak{P}(l)_+}k_\lambda=k$ and $\sum_{\lambda\in\mathfrak{P}(l)_+}kN(\lambda)=2\upsilon$, then we must have $k_1=k_\mathrm{trsp}\ge 2k-2\upsilon$. The constraint $J_l\ge 2l-2$ in Notation \ref{nota:goodconstantsIJ} will then ensure, together with Corollary \ref{cor:CHurconnected}, that $\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hur}^{\mathfrak{S}_l,\mathfrak{S}_l\setminus\mathbbl{1}}_{\underline{k},\underline{\mathbbl{1}},\mathbbl{1}}(\mathcal{F})$ is connected.

Now let $c\subseteq \mathfrak{S}_l\setminus\left\{\mathbbl{1}\right\}$ be the union of conjugacy classes $\lambda\in\mathfrak{P}(l)_+$ with $k_\lambda\ge1$, and let $c_1\subseteq c$ denote the conjugacy class of transpositions. We may identify $\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hur}^{\mathfrak{S}_l,c}_{\underline{k},\underline{\mathbbl{1}},\mathbbl{1}}(\mathcal{F})$ also as a component of $\mathrm{Hur}^{\mathfrak{S}_l,c}_k(\mathcal{F})$, which for simplicity we denote
$\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hur}^{\mathfrak{S}_l,c}_{\underline{k},\underline{\mathbbl{1}},\mathbbl{1}}(\mathcal{F})$, even though we should first remove from $\underline{k}$ all occurrences of 0. We may therefore study the map
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:ultimatetbrv}
\widetilde{\mathbf{brv}}\colon\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hur}^{\mathfrak{S}_l,c}_{\underline{k},\underline{\mathbbl{1}},\mathbbl{1}}(\mathcal{F})\to\mathrm{Conf}_{\underline{k}}(\mathcal{F}).
\end{equation}

We next recall from \cite[§2]{LL2} the notion of Hurwitz module. In particular, by \cite[Example 2.1.3]{LL2}, the sequence of sets $\mathrm{Hom}^c(\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P_m,*),\mathfrak{S}_l)$ for $m\ge0$ forms a ``bijective'' Hurwitz module over the rack $c$. We may consider the bijective Hurwitz submodule $S$ spanned by the subsets $\mathrm{Hom}^c_{\underline{\mathbbl{1}}}(\pi_1(\mathcal{F}\setminus\bar P_m,*),\mathfrak{S}_l)$, comprising group homomorphisms sending each $\delta_i\mapsto\mathbbl{1}$.
We may then identify $\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hur}^{\mathfrak{S}_l,c}_{\underline{k},\underline{\mathbbl{1}},\mathbbl{1}}(\mathcal{F})$ with a component of $\mathrm{CHur}^{c,S}_k$ in the sense of \cite{LL2}\footnote{We have been notified by the authors that the notation $\mathrm{MHur}^{c,S}_k$ shall be used in place of $\mathrm{CHur}^{c,S}$ in a forthcoming version of the article.}.

We next aim at computing the quotient module $(c/c_1,S/c_1)$ in the sense of \cite[§2.3]{LL2}. The quotient rack $c/c_1$ is the abelian rack whose elements are the conjugacy classes of $\mathfrak{S}_l$ contained in $c$; and by Lemma \ref{lem:quotientmodule} we have that $S/c_1$ has a point as $0$\textsuperscript{th} set , and therefore $(c/c_1)^m$  as $m$\textsuperscript{th} set. This implies that $\mathrm{Hur}_k^{c/c_1,S/c_1}$, in the notation of \cite{LL2}, is just $ \mathrm{Conf}_k(\mathring{\mathcal{F}},c/c_1)$, and in particular we may identify $\mathrm{Conf}_{\underline{k}}(\mathring{\mathcal{F}})$ with a connected component of $\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hur}^{c/c_1,S/c_1}$.

We may now apply \cite[Theorem 1.4.9]{LL2} and conclude that, for large enough constants $I_l,J_l$, the map \eqref{eq:ultimatetbrv} induces a rational homology equivalence in degrees $*<(k_\mathrm{trsp}-J_l)/I_l$, and in particular in degrees $*<(2k-2\upsilon-J_l)/I_l$. Concretely, we identify the source of \eqref{eq:ultimatetbrv} with a component in $\mathrm{CHur}^{c,S}$, as explained above, and identify the target of \eqref{eq:ultimatetbrv} with a component in $\mathrm{CHur}^{c/c_1,S/c_1}$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- nota-25: body_md -->
\label{nota:goodconstantsIJ}
Relying on \cite[Theorem 1.4.9]{LL2},
we fix two sequences of positive constants $I_l,J_l$, for $l\ge2$, satisfying the following properties:
\begin{itemize}
\item $I_l\ge1$ (see Lemma \ref{lem:first_reduction});
\item $J_l\ge 2l-2$ (see Corollary \ref{cor:CHurconnected});
\item for all $1\le k\le 2\upsilon$ and all $\underline{k}\in\Xi_k$ as in Notation \ref{nota:Xi}
the map
\[
\widetilde{\mathbf{brv}}\colon\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Hur}^{\mathfrak{S}_l,\mathfrak{S}_l\setminus\mathbbl{1}}_{\underline{k},\underline{\mathbbl{1}},\mathbbl{1}}(\mathcal{F})\to\mathrm{Conf}_{\underline{k}}(\mathring{\mathcal{F}})
\]
induces a rational homology isomorphism in degrees $*<(k_\mathrm{trsp}-J_l)/I_l$ (see the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:Thetaisomorphism});
\item 
both sequences $(J_l)_{l\ge2}$ and $(I_l)_{l\ge2}$ are weakly increasing with respect to divisibility: if $l,l'\ge2$ and $l\mid l'$ , then $J_l\le J_{l'}$ and $I_l\le I_{l'}$ (this is only to phrase Theorems \ref{thm:A} and \ref{thm:B} in terms of $I_d,J_d$ instead of $\max_{l\mid d}I_l,\max_{l\mid d}J_l$).
\end{itemize}
<!-- end nota-25 -->
<!-- defn-24: body_md -->
For $g\ge1$, $l\ge2$ and and $h\ge0$ we denote by $\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_h)\subseteq\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_h)$ the open substack parametrising degree $l$ maps $\theta\colon C\to D$ admitting at least one simple branch value; and we denote by $\ddot{\mathcal{H}}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_h)\subseteq\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_h)$ the open substack parametrising degree $l$ maps $\theta\colon C\to D$ that furthermore do not factor through any intermediate curve.

We similarly define, for $e\ge1$, the substacks $\ddot{\mathcal{H}}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})\subseteq\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})\subseteq\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})$ as pullbacks of the previous along the map $\varepsilon_{h,e}$. We denote by $\ddot{q}_{g,l,h,e}\colon\ddot{\mathcal{H}}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})\to\mathcal{H}_{h,e}$ the restriction of the map $q_{g,l,h,e}$ from Notation \ref{nota:qglhe}.
<!-- end defn-24 -->
<!-- lem-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:ccHcodimension}
For all $g\ge1$, $l\ge2$, $h\ge0$ and $e\ge1$ the topological stack $\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top}}$ is an oriented orbifold of real dimension $4\upsilon(h,e,0)+4\upsilon(g,l,h)-6$. Moreover, $\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top}}$ is the complement of a closed topological stubstack of codimension at least $2\upsilon(g,l,h)$ in $\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})$. 
In particular, restriction induces an isomorphism $H^*(|\mathcal{H}_{g,d}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top}}|;\mathbb{Q})\cong H^*(|\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top}}|;\mathbb{Q})$ in the range of cohomological degrees $*<2\upsilon(g,l,h)-1$.
<!-- end lem-12 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Consider the map of topological stacks $\mathrm{CBra}^{h,e}_{\mathbb{P}^{1,\mathrm{top}}}\to\mathcal{H}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}$ given by the inclusion of a fibre of the map $q_{h,e,0}^{\mathrm{top}}\colon\mathcal{H}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}\to\mathfrak{M}_0^{\mathrm{top}}$. We may pullback the smooth map $q_{g,l,h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}\colon\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top}}\to\mathcal{H}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}$ from Notation \ref{nota:qglhe} along this inclusion 
to obtain a smooth map
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:smoothpullback}    
\mathrm{CBra}^{h,e}_{\mathbb{P}^{1,\mathrm{top}}}\times_{\mathcal{H}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}}\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top}}\to \mathrm{CBra}^{h,e}_{\mathbb{P}^{1,\mathrm{top}}}
\end{equation}
whose fibre over $\theta\colon D\to \mathbb{P}^{1,\mathrm{top}}$ is $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_D$. By Proposition \ref{prop:orbifold} the base and fibre of the smooth map \eqref{eq:smoothpullback} are oriented orbifolds of dimensions $4\upsilon(h,e,0)$ and $4\upsilon(g,l,h)$, hence the fibre product in \eqref{eq:smoothpullback} is an orbifold of dimension $4\upsilon(h,e,0)+4\upsilon(g,l,h)$.
The connected Lie group $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{P}^1)^{\mathrm{top}}$ of real dimension 6 acts on the fibre product \eqref{eq:smoothpullback} with finite stabilisers, thanks to the assumptions on $g,l,h,e$ (compare with Remark \ref{rem:cHgdDMstack}). It follows that the quotient topological stack
\[
\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top}}\cong \left(\mathrm{CBra}^{h,e}_{\mathbb{P}^{1,\mathrm{top}}}\times_{\mathcal{H}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}}\mathcal{H}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top}}\right)
\ /\ \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{P}^1)^{\mathrm{top}}
\]
is an oriented orbifold of real dimension $4\upsilon(h,e,0)+4\upsilon(g,l,h)-6$.

For the second statement, it suffices to estimate codimensions on fibres of $q_{g,l,h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}$. The complement $Z$ of the intersection of $\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top}}$ with a fibre $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_D$ of $q_{g,l,h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}$ is the closed substack of 
$\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_D$ parametrising degree $l$ maps $\theta\colon C\to D$ admitting no simple branch value: if this is the case, the norm of the local monodromy of $\theta$ around each branch value of $\theta$ is at least 2, so that $\theta$ admits at most $\upsilon(g,l,h)$ branch values. It follows that 
$Z$ has real dimension at most $2\upsilon(g,l,h)$, and hence codimension at least $2\upsilon(g,l,h)$ inside $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,l}_D$.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- ex-7: body_md -->
\label{ex:ccHcH}
By Lemma \ref{lem:ccHcodimension}, the inclusion $|\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d}^{\mathrm{top}}|\hookrightarrow|\mathcal{H}_{g,d}^{\mathrm{top}}|$ induces a rational cohomology isomorphism in degrees less than $2\upsilon(g,d,0)-1=2(g+d-1)-1$. As this number is larger than the range of cohomological degrees from Theorem \ref{thm:A}, we may henceforth focus on computing the stable rational cohomology of $|\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d}^{\mathrm{top}}|$.
<!-- end ex-7 -->
<!-- lem-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:iotagdhecodimension}
The complement of the image of
$\iota_{g,d,h,e}$ has codimension at least $2\upsilon(g,d/e,h)$ inside $\ddot{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d/e}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top}}$. In particular $|\iota_{g,d,h,e}|$ induces a rational cohomology isomorphism in degrees $*<2\upsilon(g,d/e,h)-1$.
<!-- end lem-13 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
We pick $(D\to L)\in\mathcal{H}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}(*)$ and consider the 
fibre $\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,d/e}_D$ of $\ddot{q}_{g,d/e,h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}$ at $(D\to L)$. It suffices to show that the complement $Z$ of the intersection of the image of $\iota_{g,d,h,e}$ with $\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,d/e}_D$ has codimension at least $2\upsilon(g,d/e,h)$ inside $\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,d/e}_D$. If $P\subseteq D$ is the finite set of all preimages of branch values of $D\to L$ (including those that are not branch points), then $Z$ is the locus of $\mathrm{CBra}^{g,d/e}_D$ comprising maps $\theta\colon C\to D$ such that all branch values of $\theta$ belong to $P$ or are not simple branch values. The number of branch values outside $P$ can therefore be at most $\upsilon(g,d/e,h)$. It follows that $Z$ has dimension at most $2\upsilon(g,d/e,h)$ and hence codimension at least $2\upsilon(g,d/e,h)$ inside $\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,d/e}_D$.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- nota-26: body_md -->
Recall Equations \ref{eq:rvcrs} and \ref{eq:cHvcrs}. We denote by
\[
\ddot{r}_{g,l,h,e}\colon|\ddot{\mathcal{H}}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top}}_\mathrm{vcrs}|\to|\mathcal{H}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}|
\]
the pullback along $|\varepsilon_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}|$ of the projection
\[
|\ddot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{Bra}^{g,l}_\Sigma|\sslash\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma)\to\mathbf{B}\mathrm{Homeo}^+(\Sigma)\simeq|\mathfrak{M}_h^{\mathrm{top}}|,
\]
where $\Sigma$ is a connected closed oriented surface of genus $h$.
<!-- end nota-26 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Recall Notation \ref{nota:intfp}, and abbreviate $\upsilon=\upsilon(g,d/e,h)$.
By Theorem \ref{thm:Thetaisomorphism} and Corollary \ref{cor:defnTheta} the following composite map of parametrised rational spectra over $\mathcal{H}_{h,e}$ induces a fibrewise isomorphism on homotopy groups $\pi_*$ in degrees $*>-(2\upsilon-J_{d/e})/I_{d/e}$:
\[
\left(\int_{|\mathfrak{p}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}|}\mathcal{A}(d/e)\right)_{2\upsilon}\xrightarrow{\Theta^{g,d/e}_{h,e}[-4\upsilon]}(r_{g,d/e,h,e})*\mathbb{Q}\to (\ddot{r}_{g,d/e,h,e})_*\mathbb{Q}.
\]
We may then apply $|\mathcal{H}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}|_*$ to the previous and obtain a map of rational spectra 
\[
|\mathcal{H}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}|_*\left(\int_{|\mathfrak{p}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}|}\mathcal{A}(d/e)\right)_{2\upsilon}\to|\ddot{\mathcal{H}}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top}}_\mathrm{vcrs}|_*\mathbb{Q}
\]
which induces an isomorphism on homotopy groups in the same range. The last map may now be composed
with the maps
\[
|\ddot{\mathcal{H}}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top}}_\mathrm{vcrs}|_*\mathbb{Q}\xrightarrow{\simeq}|\ddot{\mathcal{H}}_{g,l}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top}}|_*\mathbb{Q}\xrightarrow{|\iota_{g,d,h,e}|}|\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d}^{\mathrm{top}}|_*\mathbb{Q}
\]
where the first is an equivalence as observed in 
\eqref{eq:diagramdrQequivalence}, whereas the second is an equivalence in the large range of homotopy groups $*>2\upsilon-1$ by Lemma \ref{lem:iotagdhecodimension}.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- nota-27: body_md -->
We denote by $\bar\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top}}$ the closure of the stratum $\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top}}$ inside
$\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top}}$. Similarly, we denote by 
$\bar\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\mathcal{H}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top}}$ the closure of the subspace $\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top}}$ inside
$\mathcal{H}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top}}$. It is the locus of those equivalence classes of degree $d$ maps $\theta\colon C\to L$ that admit some factorisation through a degree $e$ map $D\to L$.
<!-- end nota-27 -->
<!-- lem-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:surjectivecollapse}
The collapse map
\[
H_*(|(\bar\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top}})^\infty|,\infty;\mathbb{Q})\to H_*(|(\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top}})^\infty|,\infty;\mathbb{Q})
\]
is surjective in the range of homological degrees
\[
*>\dim(\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d}^{\mathrm{top}})-\ (2\upsilon(g,d/e,h)-J_{d/e})/I_{d/e}
\]
and in particular in the range $*>\dim(\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d}^{\mathrm{top}})-(2(g+d-1)-J_d)/I_d$.
<!-- end lem-14 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Abbreviate by $\delta$ the (real) dimension of $\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d}$.
By Lemma \ref{lem:iotagdhecodimension} and by the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:B}, the composition of the two top horizonal maps and the right vertical map
in the following diagram is surjective in homology relative to $\infty$ in the first given range of degrees, since its precomposition with the map $|\mathcal{H}_{h,e}^{\mathrm{top}}|_*\Theta^{g,d/e}_{h,e}[\delta]$ from Notation \ref{nota:intfp} is an isomorphism:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:compositecollapse}
\begin{tikzcd}
{|\mathcal{H}_{g,d/e}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top},\infty}_\mathrm{vcrs}|}\ar[r,"\simeq_\mathbb{Q}"] & {|\mathcal{H}_{g,d/e}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top},\infty}_\mathrm{crs}|}\ar[r]\ar[dl,dashed]&{ |\ddot{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d/e}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top},\infty}_\mathrm{crs}|}\ar[d,"|\iota_{g,d,h,e,\mathrm{crs}}|"]\\
{|(\bar\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\mathcal{H}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top}})^\infty|}\ar[r]&{|(\bar\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top}})^\infty|}\ar[r]&{|(\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top}})^\infty|}.
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
All horizonal maps in the pentagon are collapse maps corresponding to open inclusions.
The dashed diagonal map is constructed as follows: we have a proper forgetful map $\mathcal{H}_{g,d/e}(\mathfrak{p}_{h,e})^{\mathrm{top}}_\mathrm{crs}\to\mathcal{H}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top}}$ sending the class of $(C\to D\to L)$ to the class of $(C\to L)$. Its image is contained in (in fact, equal to) $\bar\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\mathcal{H}_{g,d}$, and we consider the associated map on one point compactifications. The pentagon commutes by inspection; it follows that the bottom right horizontal collapse map is also surjective in the first given range of homological degrees.

For the final statement, we observe that the first given range of homological degrees $\dim(\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d}^{\mathrm{top}})-\ (2\upsilon(g,d/e,h)-J_{d/e})/I_{d/e}$ may be rewritten as the expression 
$\dim(\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d}^{\mathrm{top}})-4\rho(h,e,d)-(2\upsilon(g,d/e,h)-J_{d/e})/I_{d/e}$,
and we have inequalities
\[
\begin{split}
&4\rho(h,e,d)+(2\upsilon(g,d/e,h)-J_{d/e})/I_{d/e}\\
\ge&4(h+e-1)(d/e-1)+(2(g-1)-2(h-1)d/e-J_d)/I_d\\
\ge&4(e-1)(d/e-1)+(2(g-1)+2d/e-J_d)/I_d\\
\ge&(2(g+d-1)-J_d)/I_d,
\end{split}
\]
where we used the fourth property in Notation \ref{nota:goodconstantsIJ}, the fact that the second expression is mimimized for $h=0$, and the fact that the third expression is minimized, among values of $e$ between $1$ and $d/2$, for $e=1$.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
We filter the pointed space $\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top},\infty}$  by suitable unions of its closed pointed subspaces $(\bar\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top}})^\infty$: for $k\ge1$ we denote by $S_k$ the set of pairs $(h,e)$ where $h\ge0$ is arbitrary, and $e\mid d$ is a divisor such that $d/e$ factors as a product of exactly $k$ prime numbers. We then let
$F_k\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top},\infty}$ be the union of all subspaces $(\bar\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top}})^\infty$ corresponding to pairs $(h,e)\in S_{k'}$ for some $k'\le k$. We also set $F_0\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top},\infty}=\left\{\infty\right\}$.
We thus obtain an increasing filtration of $\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top},\infty}$ by closed pointed subspaces. We may then run a spectral sequence to compute the homology of $\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top},\infty}$. By Lemma \ref{lem:surjectivecollapse}, the composite map
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
\bigoplus_{(h,e)\in S_k}H_*(|(\bar\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top}})^\infty|,\infty;\mathbb{Q})\ar[r]& H_*(|F_k\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top},\infty}|,\infty;\mathbb{Q})\ar[dl]\\
H_*(|F_k\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top},\infty}|,|F_{k-1}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top},\infty}|;\mathbb{Q})\ar[r,"\cong"]& \bigoplus_{(h,e)\in S_k}H_*(|(\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top}})^\infty|,\infty;\mathbb{Q})
\end{tikzcd}
\]
is surjective in homological degrees $*> \dim(\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d}^{\mathrm{top}})-(2(g+d-1)-J_d)/I_d$; in particular the diagonal map is also surjective in the same range.  
It follows that the spectral sequence collapses in this range of degrees, in which we obtain isomorphisms
\[
H_*(|\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d,\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top},\infty}|,\infty;\mathbb{Q})\cong \bigoplus_{\overset{h\ge0}{1\le e<d,\ e\mid d}}H_*(|(\mathfrak{F}_{h,e}\check{\mathcal{H}}_{g,d\mathrm{crs}}^{\mathrm{top}})^\infty|,\infty;\mathbb{Q}).
\]
The statement of Theorem \ref{thm:A} now follows
by Poincar\'e--Lefschetz duality.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- nota-28: body_md -->
\label{nota:FSlek}
For $k\ge0$ we denote by $\mathrm{FS}^{\le k}\subseteq\mathrm{FS}$ the (possibly empty) full subcategory spanned by finite sets of cardinality at most $k$.
<!-- end nota-28 -->
<!-- defn-25: body_md -->
\label{defn:xiclass}
Recall Notation \ref{nota:universal_curve}. We denote by 
\[
\xi_{l,h}\in H^0\left(|\mathfrak{M}_h^{\mathrm{top}}|;\int_{|\mathfrak{p}_h^{\mathrm{top}}|}\mathcal{A}(l)\right)_1
\]
the class corresponding to the composite map of rational spectra
\[
\mathbb{Q}\xrightarrow{1}|\mathcal{C}_h^{\mathrm{top}}|_*\mathbb{Q}\simeq|\mathfrak{M}_h^{\mathrm{top}}|_*|\mathfrak{p}_h^{\mathrm{top}}|_*\mathbb{Q}\simeq |\mathfrak{M}_h^{\mathrm{top}}|_*\left(\int_{|\mathfrak{p}^{\mathrm{top}}|}\mathcal{A}(l)\right)_1,
\]
where the first map labeled ``1'' is the unit.
<!-- end defn-25 -->
<!-- nota-29: body_md -->
\label{nota:intfiltration}
Recall Notation \ref{nota:FSlek}. For a connected homotopy type $Y$, a presentably symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category $\mathcal{C}$ and a non-unital symmetric monoidal functor $I\colon \mathrm{FS}\to\mathcal{C}$, we filter $\int_YI$ by the graded spectra
\[
F_k\int_YI\coloneqq \operatorname{colim}_{\mathrm{FS}^{\le k}_{/Y}}I\in\mathcal{C},\quad k\ge0.
\]
We obtain a refinement of $\int_YI$ to a commutative algebra in $\mathbb{N}_{\le}$-filtered objects in $\mathcal{C}$, i.e. in the functor category $\mathrm{Fun}(\mathbb{N}_{\le},\mathcal{C})$ with Day convolution.
<!-- end nota-29 -->
<!-- defn-26: body_md -->
\label{defn:cAfiltration}
Recall Definition \ref{defn:cAheart}. We consider the two-step filtration on $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)$ given by $F_0\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)=\mathbb{Q}\cdot[\! [\mathbbl{1}]\! ]$ and $F_k\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)=\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)$ for $k\ge1$. It makes $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)$ into a commutative algebra in $\mathrm{Fun}(\mathbb{N}_{\le},\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}^\mathbb{N})$. We denote by 
\[
\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)^\delta\coloneqq\bigoplus_{k\ge0} (F_k/F_{k-1})\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l).
\]
the associated graded algebra: it is a commutative algebra in $\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}}_\mathbb{Q}$.
We also consider $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)_+^\delta$ as a non-unital commutative algebra in $\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}^{\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}}$.
<!-- end defn-26 -->
<!-- defn-27: body_md -->
\label{defn:Confmonoid}
Recall Definition \ref{defn:colconf}. For a finite set $S$ endowed with a grading $N\colon S\to\mathbb{N}$ and for a topological space $X$ we consider the disjoint union
\[
\mathrm{Conf}(X,S)\coloneqq\coprod_{k\ge0}\mathrm{Conf}_k(X,S)
\]
as a bigraded topological space: a pair $(P,f)$ of a finite set $P$ with a map $f\colon P\to S$ is in bigrading $(\#P,\sum_{z\in P}N(f(z)))$.

When $X$ is a compact topological space, by taking one point compactifications in each bigrading, we obtain a bigraded pointed topological space
\[
\mathrm{Conf}(X,S)^\infty\coloneqq\bigvee_{k\ge0}\mathrm{Conf}_k(X,S)^\infty.
\]
<!-- end defn-27 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Consider the element $\xi_{l,h}[2]\in\pi_2(\int_{|\Sigma|}\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l))_1\cong \pi_2(|\Sigma|_!\mathbb{Q})$ corresponding to $\xi_{l,h}$. In few words, $\xi_{l,h}[2]$ is the fundamental class of $\Sigma$. It suffices to prove that the map
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:firstTheoremD}  
\xi_{l,h}[2]\cdot -\colon \left(\int_{|\Sigma|}\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)\right)_n[2]\to \left(\int_{|\Sigma|}\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)\right)_{n+1}
\end{equation}
induces an isomorphism on $\pi_*$ in degrees $*>-n+2(n+1)=n+2$. For $n=0$ we just observe that the map $\mathbb{Q}[2]\to|\Sigma|_!\mathbb{Q}$ giving the fundamental class induces an isomorphism between vanishing homotopy groups in degrees $*>2$.

From now on we suppose $n\ge1$: this allows us to replace $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)$ by $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)_+$ in \eqref{eq:firstTheoremD}; moreover, since \eqref{eq:firstTheoremD} is a filtered map, as observed in \eqref{eq:xilhfiltered}, it suffices to prove for all $k\ge0$ that the associated graded map
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:secondTheoremD}  
\xi_{l,h}[2]\cdot -\colon (F_k/F_{k-1})\left(\int_{|\Sigma|}\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)\right)_n[2]\to (F_{k+1}/F_k)\left(\int_{|\Sigma|}\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)\right)_{n+1}
\end{equation}
induces an isomorphism on $\pi_*$ for $*>n+2$. By the previous discussion, it is equivalent to ask whether for all $k\ge0$ the map
\[
H_{i-2}(\mathrm{Conf}_k(\Sigma,\mathfrak{P}(l)_+)_n^\infty,\infty;\mathbb{Q})\to H_{i}(\mathrm{Conf}_{k+1}(\Sigma,\mathfrak{P}(l)_+)_{n+1}^\infty,\infty;\mathbb{Q})
\]
given by superposition with the fundamental class of $\mathrm{Conf}_1(\Sigma,\left\{\mathrm{trsp}\right\})\cong \Sigma$ induces an isomorphism for $i>n+2$. If $2k+1\le n$, this holds true because the above homology groups vanish for dimension reasons. Otherwise, if $\underline{k}=(k_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\mathfrak{P}(l)_+}$ satisfies $\sum_{\lambda\in\mathfrak{P}(l)_+} k_\lambda=k$ and $\sum_{\lambda\in\mathfrak{P}(l)_+} k_\lambda N(\lambda)=n$, then we may define $\underline{k}'$ by replacing $k_\mathrm{trsp}$ with $k'_\mathrm{trsp}=k_\mathrm{trsp}+1$, and the previous map restricts to a map
\[
H_{i-2}(\mathrm{Conf}_{\underline{k}}(\Sigma)^\infty,\infty;\mathbb{Q})\to H_{i}(\mathrm{Conf}_{\underline{k}'}(\Sigma)^\infty,\infty;\mathbb{Q})
\]
which by 
\cite{Church} (see in particular \cite[Theorem 1.3]{Knudsen}, and the discussion in \cite[§2.3]{ORW2}) induces an isomorphism for $i>2k-k_1$, and in particular for $i>n$. Note also that every $\underline{k}'$ with $\sum k'_\lambda=k+1$ and $\sum k'_\lambda N(\lambda)=n+1$ must satisfy  $k'_\mathrm{trsp}\ge1$, otherwise we would have $n\ge 2k+1$.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- defn-28: body_md -->
For a space $X$ and for $k\ge0$ we denote by $\mathrm{SP}(X)_k= X^k/\mathfrak{S}_k$ the $k$\textsuperscript{th} symmetric power of $X$; here the quotient is strict. We regard $\mathrm{SP}(X)\coloneqq \coprod_{k\ge0}\mathrm{SP}(X)_k$ as the free strictly commutative topological monoid generated by $X$. Its elements may be written as formal sums $\sum_{i=1}^nk_i\cdot x_i$, with $n\ge0$, distinct points $x_1,\dots,x_n$, and coefficients $k_1,\dots,k_n\ge1$.

Similarly, for a finite set $S$, we regard $\mathrm{SP}(X)^S\cong\mathrm{SP}(X\times S)$ as the free strictly commutative topological monoid generated by $X\times S$. Its elements take the form $\sum_{i=1}^n\underline{k}_i\cdot x_i$, where the points $x_i$ are still distinct, but now now $\underline{k}_i\in\mathbb{N}^S\setminus\underline{0}$.

If moreover $\mathcal{I}\subseteq\mathbb{N}^S$ is an ideal (i.e. $\underline{0}\notin\mathcal{I}$, and the sum $\underline{k}+\underline{k}'$ belongs to $\mathcal{I}$ as soon as either $\underline{k}$ or $\underline{k}$ belongs to $\mathcal{I}$), then the difference $\mathbb{N}^S\setminus\mathcal{I}$ is a partial abelian monoid, and we define
\[
\mathrm{Conf}(X,\mathbb{N}^S\setminus\mathcal{I})=\coprod_{\underline{k}\in\mathbb{N}^S}\mathrm{Conf}(X,\mathbb{N}^S\setminus\mathcal{I})_{\underline{k}}\subseteq\mathrm{SP}(X)^S=\coprod_{\underline{k}\in\mathbb{N}^S}\mathrm{SP}(X)_{\underline{k}}
\]
as the subspace comprising those formal sums $\sum_{i=1}^n\underline{k}_i\cdot x_i$ with all coefficients $\underline{k}_i\in\mathbb{N}^S\setminus \mathcal{I}$. We regard $\mathrm{Conf}(X,\mathbb{N}^S\setminus\mathcal{I})$ as an $\mathbb{N}^S$-graded space. When $X$ is a compact topological space, by taking one point compactifications in a $\mathbb{N}^S$-graded fashion, we obtain the $\mathbb{N}^S$-graded pointed space
\[
\mathrm{Conf}(X,\mathbb{N}^S\setminus\mathcal{I})^\infty\coloneqq\bigvee_{\underline{k}\in\mathbb{N}^S}\mathrm{Conf}(X,\mathbb{N}^S\setminus\mathcal{I})_{\underline{k}}^\infty;
\]
we may regard it as the quotient of $\mathrm{SP}(X)^S$ by the topological ideal spanned by those elements $\sum_{i=1}^n\underline{k}_i\cdot x_i$ with at least one $\underline{k}_i\in\mathcal{I}$.
<!-- end defn-28 -->
<!-- rem-18: body_md -->
\label{rem:SPmanifolds}
If $\Sigma$ is an oriented topological surface, then $\mathrm{SP}(\Sigma)_k$ is an oriented topological $2k$-manifold,
and $\mathrm{SP}(\Sigma)_{\underline{k}}\subseteq\mathrm{SP}(\Sigma)^S$, as well as its open subsets of the form $\mathrm{Conf}(\Sigma,\mathbb{N}^S\setminus\mathcal{I})_{\underline{k}}$, are  oriented topological manifolds of dimension $2\sum_{s\in S}k_s$.
<!-- end rem-18 -->
<!-- ex-8: body_md -->
\label{ex:intConfidentification}
We have used the above identification in Subsection \ref{subsec:proofthmD} for $X=\Sigma$, $S=\mathfrak{P}(l)_+$ and $\mathcal{I}\subseteq\mathbb{N}^S$ being the ideal of all $\underline{k}$ with $\sum_\lambda k_\lambda\ge2$. In this case $\mathrm{Conf}(X,\mathbb{N}^S\setminus\mathcal{I})\cong\mathrm{Conf}(X,S)$.
<!-- end ex-8 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
By \cite[Proposition 6.1]{BCP:Hilb}, there are isomorphisms of commutative algebras in $\mathrm{Vec}_\mathbb{Q}^\mathbb{N}$ of the form $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(2)\cong\mathbb{Q}[x]/x^2$, $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(3)\cong\mathbb{Q}[x]/x^3$, $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(4)\cong\mathbb{Q}[x,y]/(x^3-4xy,x^4,y^2)$ and $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(5)\cong\mathbb{Q}[x,y]/(x^4-5x^2y,x^4-25y^2,x^5)$. In all cases $x$ has grading $1$ and $y$ has grading $2$ with respect to the grading induced by the norm. A change of variables $(x,y)\mapsto(x,x^2-4y)$ leads to an isomorphism $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(4)\cong\mathbb{Q}[x,y]/(x^4,xy,y^2)$; similarly, a change of variables $(x,y)\mapsto(x,x^2-5y)$ leads to an isomorphism $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(5)\cong\mathbb{Q}[x,y]/(x^5,x^2y,y^2)$. We have thus found a monomial presentation for $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)$ for $l\le5$. Precisely, we have identified $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)\cong\mathbb{Q}[\mathbb{N}]/(\mathbb{N}\setminus M_l)$ for $l=2,3$, and $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)\cong\mathbb{Q}[\mathbb{N}^2]/(\mathbb{N}^2\setminus M_l)$ for $l=4,5$. This perspective suggests to change our notion of grading in the two cases $l=4,5$: instead of the single $\mathbb{N}$-grading coming from the norm of permutations, we consider in the following on $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(4)$ and $\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(5)$ a bigrading coming from declaring $x$ to be in bigrading $(1,0)$ and $y$ to be in bigrading $(0,1)$.
We may now deduce the following equivalences of commutative algebras in $\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}^\mathbb{N}$ (for $l=2,3$) or $\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}^{\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}}$ (for $l=4,5$)
\[
\int_{|\Sigma|}\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)\simeq \left(|\mathrm{Conf}(\Sigma,M_l)^\infty|,\infty\right)_!\mathbb{Q},\quad l=2,3,4,5.
\]
We would now like to deduce a formula for $\int_{|\Sigma|}\mathcal{A}(l)$. For $l=2,3$ we just operate the endofunctor $\mathrm{sh}$ from Remark \ref{rem:evenshift}: using Remark \ref{rem:SPmanifolds} we obtain for $n\ge0$ the identification of $|\mathrm{Conf}(\Sigma,M_l)_n^\infty|_*\mathbb{Q}
$ with
\[
(|\mathrm{Conf}(\Sigma,M_l)_n^\infty|,\infty)_!\mathbb{Q}[-2n]\simeq 
\left(\int_{|\Sigma|}\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)\right)_n[-2n]\simeq
\left(\int_{|\Sigma|}\mathcal{A}(l)\right)_n.
\]
For $l=4,5$ we operate the endofunctor of $\mathrm{Sp}_\mathbb{Q}^{\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}}$ sending $(\omega_{a,b})_{(a,b)\in\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}}$ to the object $(\omega_{a,b}\ [-2a-4b])_{(a,b)\in\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}}$. For $a,b\ge0$, this allows us to identify the shift $|\mathrm{Conf}(\Sigma;M_l)_{a,b}|_*\mathbb{Q}\ [-2b]$ with
\[
\left(|\mathrm{Conf}(\Sigma;M_l)^\infty_{a,b}|,\infty\right)_!\mathbb{Q}\ [-2a-4b]\simeq 
\left(\int_{|\Sigma|}\mathcal{A}^\heartsuit(l)\right)_{a,b}[-2a-4b]\simeq
\left(\int_{|\Sigma|}\mathcal{A}(l)\right)_{a,b}.
\]
<!-- end proof-21 -->
